zh.Collocation: a difference may “result fr: 固定搭配：差異可能 result from（源自）某個原因，這裡指好幾代與人類為鄰的生活。差異不能 benefit、suffer 或 escape from 世代。
zh.The colon introduces opposing views — so: 冒號引出了對立的看法——有人餵食、有人視為害獸——這正是 controversial（具爭議性）的意思。extinct 和 invisible 都與「存在」相矛盾。

questions.title: The minimum wage debate
parts: For decades, textbook economics predicted that raising the minimum wage would
jobs, since employers would hire fewer workers at a higher price. In the 1990s, a study comparing fast-food restaurants on either side of a state border found no such
after one state raised its minimum wage. The finding
a long and often heated debate that lasted more than twenty years. Most economists now accept that moderate increases have little effect on employment, though very large rises could still
harm, particularly in low-wage regions.
why: “employers would hire fewer workers” means jobs would be lost, so the prediction was that a higher minimum wage would destroy jobs. “create” is the opposite.
The study looked for the predicted job losses and did not find them: “no such effect”. The other nouns do not refer back to the prediction.
A debate that then “lasted more than twenty years” was started by the finding, so it sparked it. “ended”, “avoided” and “prevented” contradict the debate continuing.
Collocation: cause harm. You do not “take”, “keep” or “hold” harm.

zh.For decades, textbook economics predicte: 數十年來，教科書中的經濟學預測，提高最低工資會 ____ 工作機會，因為在價格較高的情況下，雇主會雇用較少的員工。1990 年代，一項比較州界兩側速食店的研究發現，在其中一州提高最低工資後，並沒有出現這樣的 ____ 。這項發現 ____ 了一場持續二十多年、經常很激烈的辯論。大多數經濟學家現在認為，適度的調漲對就業影響不大，不過非常大幅的調漲仍可能 ____ 傷害，尤其是在低工資地區。
zh.“employers would hire fewer workers” mea: 「雇主會雇用較少的員工」表示工作會減少，所以預測是提高最低工資會 destroy（摧毀）工作機會。create 則正好相反。
zh.The study looked for the predicted job l: 這項研究尋找預測中的就業減少，卻沒有找到：no such effect（沒有這樣的影響）。其他名詞都無法指回那個預測。
zh.A debate that then “lasted more than twe: 一場之後「持續二十多年」的辯論，是由這項發現引起的，所以是 sparked（引發）。ended、avoided 和 prevented 都與辯論持續進行相矛盾。
zh.Collocation: cause harm. You do not “tak: 固定搭配：cause harm（造成傷害）。英文不說 take、keep 或 hold harm。

questions.title: Second life for car batteries
parts: Electric cars depend on lithium-ion batteries, which contain valuable metals such as lithium, cobalt and nickel. When a car battery can no longer hold enough
for driving, it often still has around seventy per cent of its original capacity, so it can be
for less demanding uses, such as storing solar power in homes. Eventually, however, the cells must be recycled. Current methods can
most of the metals, but they are energy-intensive, and researchers are trying to design batteries that are easier to take
why: A battery holds charge, and that is what fades as it ages. Batteries do not “hold enough weight, speed or heat” for driving.
A battery with seventy per cent capacity left can be reused for lighter tasks such as home solar storage. Nothing suggests it is repaired, and “rejected” contradicts the uses described.
Recycling aims to get the metals back: to recover them. Wasting or ignoring them is the opposite, and metals cannot be invented.
Phrasal verb: “take apart” means dismantle, which recycling requires. “take over”, “take off” and “take up” mean something quite different.

zh.Electric cars depend on lithium-ion batt: 電動車仰賴鋰離子電池，而電池中含有鋰、鈷和鎳等珍貴金屬。當汽車電池再也無法儲存足夠的 ____ 供行車使用時，它通常仍保有原始容量的百分之七十左右，所以可以被 ____ 於要求較低的用途，例如在家中儲存太陽能電力。然而，最終這些電池芯還是必須回收。目前的方法可以 ____ 大部分的金屬，但耗能很高，因此研究人員正試圖設計更容易 ____ 的電池。
zh.A battery holds charge, and that is what: 電池儲存的是 charge（電量），而這正是隨著老化而衰退的東西。電池不會為行車「儲存足夠的重量、速度或熱量」。
zh.A battery with seventy per cent capacity: 仍保有七成容量的電池可以被 reused（再利用）於較輕的用途，例如家用太陽能儲電。文中沒有提到修理，而 rejected 與文中描述的用途相矛盾。
zh.Recycling aims to get the metals back: t: 回收的目的是取回金屬：recover（回收、取回）。浪費或忽視金屬正好相反，而金屬也無法被發明。
zh.Phrasal verb: “take apart” means dismant: 片語動詞：take apart（拆解），這正是回收所需要的。take over、take off 和 take up 的意思完全不同。

questions.title: The Hanseatic League
parts: From the thirteenth to the fifteenth century, the Hanseatic League linked dozens of trading towns around the Baltic and North Sea. It was not a state but a
of merchants and cities that cooperated to protect their trade. Members shared
, set common standards for goods and, when necessary, organised boycotts against rulers who threatened their interests. The League’s power
as strong territorial states emerged and new trade routes shifted business towards the Atlantic, but several of its towns still
the title Hanseatic City today.
why: The sentence contrasts “not a state” with a looser structure of cooperating members: a network. “a state” repeats what the sentence denies, and a ruler or religion does not describe cooperating cities.
Members cooperated in practical ways, such as sharing information about prices and routes. Weather, ancestors and holidays are not things traders can decide to share.
New states emerging and trade moving to the Atlantic are causes of weakness, so the League’s power declined. The other verbs describe growth or return.
Collocation: a town “carries” a title, meaning it still holds it. “still lose”, “refuse” or “spend the title today” makes no sense.

zh.From the thirteenth to the fifteenth cen: 從十三世紀到十五世紀，漢薩同盟把波羅的海和北海周圍數十個貿易城鎮連結在一起。它不是一個國家，而是一個由商人和城市組成、為保護貿易而合作的 ____ 。成員之間共享 ____ ，為商品制定共同標準，必要時還會對威脅其利益的統治者發起抵制。隨著強大的領土國家興起，新的貿易路線又把生意轉向大西洋，同盟的勢力逐漸 ____ ，但它的一些城鎮至今仍 ____ 「漢薩城市」的稱號。
zh.The sentence contrasts “not a state” wit: 這句話把「不是一個國家」和一個由合作成員組成的鬆散結構對比：network（網絡）。state 重複了句子所否定的東西，而 ruler 或 religion 都無法描述互相合作的城市。
zh.Members cooperated in practical ways, su: 成員以實際的方式合作，例如分享價格和路線的 information（資訊）。天氣、祖先和假日都不是商人能決定分享的東西。
zh.New states emerging and trade moving to: 新國家興起和貿易轉向大西洋都是衰弱的原因，所以同盟的勢力 declined（衰退）。其他動詞描述的是成長或回歸。
zh.Collocation: a town “carries” a title, m: 固定搭配：城鎮 carries（擁有、保有）某個稱號。「至今仍失去、拒絕或花費這個稱號」都說不通。

questions.title: The value of wetlands
parts: Wetlands were long regarded as wasteland, and across Europe and North America more than half of them were
for farming or building. Scientists now recognise that they provide valuable services. A wetland acts like a sponge,
excess water during storms and releasing it slowly, which reduces flooding downstream. Wetland plants also filter pollutants, and peat bogs store more carbon per hectare than most
. Restoring wetlands is therefore increasingly seen as a cheap way to
against both floods and climate change.
why: Turning a wetland into farmland means removing its water, which is draining it. “protected” contradicts “regarded as wasteland”, and a wetland is already wet, so “flooded” makes no sense.
A sponge absorbs water: the wetland takes in storm water and releases it slowly. The other verbs do not describe holding water.
The comparison is with other natural carbon stores, and forests are the obvious benchmark. Factories, engines and roads release carbon rather than storing it.
Collocation: “insure against” a risk, meaning protect yourself from it. “compete”, “argue” and “vote against” do not describe protection from floods.

zh.Wetlands were long regarded as wasteland: 濕地長久以來被視為荒地，在歐洲和北美，超過一半的濕地被 ____ 以供耕作或建築使用。科學家現在認識到，濕地提供了寶貴的功能。濕地就像一塊海綿，在暴風雨期間 ____ 多餘的水，再慢慢釋放出來，減少下游的洪水。濕地植物還能過濾污染物，而泥炭沼澤每公頃儲存的碳比大多數 ____ 還多。因此，恢復濕地越來越被視為一種 ____ 洪水和氣候變遷的低成本方法。
zh.Turning a wetland into farmland means re: 把濕地變成農田就是移除其中的水，也就是 drained（排乾）。protected 與「被視為荒地」相矛盾，而濕地本來就是濕的，所以 flooded 說不通。
zh.A sponge absorbs water: the wetland take: 海綿會 absorb（吸收）水：濕地吸收暴雨的水再慢慢釋放。其他動詞都無法描述蓄水的作用。
zh.The comparison is with other natural car: 這裡比較的是其他天然的碳儲存庫，而 forests（森林）是最明顯的比較基準。工廠、引擎和道路會排放碳，而不是儲存碳。
zh.Collocation: “insure against” a risk, me: 固定搭配：insure against（防範）某種風險，也就是保護自己免受其害。compete、argue 和 vote against 都無法描述防範洪水。

questions.title: Music lessons and the brain
parts: It is often claimed that learning a musical instrument makes children more intelligent. Brain scans do show that musicians have
differences in areas involved in hearing and movement. However, controlled trials, in which children are randomly
to music lessons or another activity, have found little effect on general intelligence or school results. The benefits appear to be more
: musical training improves musical skills and perhaps some aspects of listening, but it is not a
to broader academic ability.
why: Brain scans detect the differences, so they are measurable. “invisible” and “imaginary” contradict what the scans show.
Randomised trials assign children to groups at random, which is what makes them controlled. “invited” and “paid” do not describe random allocation.
The colon lists narrow effects on musical skill and listening, so the benefits are specific. “general” contradicts “little effect on general intelligence”.
The point is that music is not a quick route to wider academic gains: it is not a shortcut to them. Reply, sequel and receipt make no sense with “to broader academic ability”.

zh.It is often claimed that learning a musi: 人們常說學習樂器能讓孩子變得更聰明。腦部掃描確實顯示，音樂家在負責聽覺和動作的腦區中有 ____ 的差異。然而，把孩子隨機 ____ 到音樂課或其他活動的對照試驗，發現這對一般智力或學業成績的影響很小。音樂訓練的好處似乎比較 ____ ：它能提升音樂技能，或許也能改善某些方面的聽力，但它並不是通往更廣泛學業能力的 ____ 。
zh.Brain scans detect the differences, so t: 腦部掃描偵測到了這些差異，所以它們是 measurable（可測量的）。invisible 和 imaginary 都與掃描結果相矛盾。
zh.Randomised trials assign children to gro: 隨機試驗會把孩子隨機 assigned（分派）到不同組別，這正是對照試驗的特點。invited 和 paid 都無法描述隨機分配。
zh.The colon lists narrow effects on musica: 冒號後面列出的是對音樂技能和聽力的狹窄影響，所以好處是 specific（特定的）。general 與「對一般智力影響很小」相矛盾。
zh.The point is that music is not a quick r: 重點在於音樂並不是通往更廣泛學業成就的快速途徑：它不是一條 shortcut（捷徑）。reply、sequel 和 receipt 搭配「通往更廣泛的學業能力」都說不通。

questions.title: Finding lost cities with lasers
parts: For centuries, dense jungle hid the ruins of ancient Maya cities in Central America. Lidar, a technique that fires laser pulses from an aircraft and
how long they take to bounce back, has changed that. By filtering out the signals reflected by leaves, researchers can create detailed maps of the ground beneath the
. Surveys have revealed tens of thousands of previously unknown structures, suggesting that the Maya population was far
than once believed. The technique does not replace excavation, but it tells archaeologists where to
why: Lidar works by timing the reflections, so it measures how long they take. Guessing or ignoring the time would produce no map.
“signals reflected by leaves” points to the layer of treetops above the ground: the canopy. The passage is about jungle, not an ocean, desert or city.
Tens of thousands of new structures imply more people, so the population was larger than believed. “smaller” reverses the evidence.
Excavation means digging, and lidar shows archaeologists where to dig. The other verbs have nothing to do with excavation.

zh.For centuries, dense jungle hid the ruin: 數個世紀以來，茂密的叢林掩蓋了中美洲古代馬雅城市的遺跡。光達是一種從飛機上發射雷射脈衝、並 ____ 脈衝反彈回來所需時間的技術，它改變了這種情況。研究人員濾除樹葉反射的訊號後，就能繪製出 ____ 下方地面的詳細地圖。調查發現了數以萬計過去未知的建築，顯示馬雅人口遠比過去認為的 ____ 。這項技術並不能取代挖掘，但它能告訴考古學家該在哪裡 ____ 。
zh.Lidar works by timing the reflections, s: 光達的原理是計算反射的時間，所以它 measures（測量）反彈所需的時間。猜測或忽略時間都無法產生地圖。
zh.“signals reflected by leaves” points to: 「被樹葉反射的訊號」指的是地面上方的樹頂層：canopy（樹冠層）。這篇文章談的是叢林，而不是海洋、沙漠或城市。
zh.Tens of thousands of new structures impl: 數以萬計的新建築意味著人口更多，所以人口比過去認為的 larger（更多）。smaller 把證據顛倒了。
zh.Excavation means digging, and lidar show: 挖掘就是 dig（挖），而光達告訴考古學家該在哪裡挖。其他動詞都與挖掘無關。

questions.title: Why expectations matter for inflation
parts: Central banks pay close attention not only to current inflation but also to what people
it to be in the future. If workers believe prices will rise quickly, they ask for larger pay increases, and firms raise prices in
, which can make the belief come true. For this reason, central banks try to keep expectations
by stating a clear inflation target and acting consistently. When that credibility is lost, bringing inflation back
can require much higher interest rates.
why: The topic is expectations, and “what people expect it to be in the future” is the natural construction. “remember” refers to the past, and “prefer” and “forbid” are not predictions.
Fixed phrase: “in anticipation” means in advance of something expected. Firms raise prices because they anticipate rises; the other nouns do not form a fitting phrase.
Economists say expectations are “anchored” when they stay steady around the target, which is the aim of a clear target. Hidden, doubled or reversed expectations are not.
Phrasal verb: “bring inflation back down” to the target. “out”, “away” and “off” do not express reducing it.

zh.Central banks pay close attention not on: 中央銀行不僅密切關注目前的通貨膨脹，也關注人們 ____ 未來的通膨會是多少。如果勞工相信物價會迅速上漲，他們就會要求更高的加薪，而企業也會 ____ 地提高價格，這可能讓這種信念成真。因此，中央銀行會透過明確的通膨目標和一致的行動，努力讓預期保持 ____ 。一旦失去了這種公信力，要把通膨重新 ____ 可能需要高得多的利率。
zh.The topic is expectations, and “what peo: 主題是預期，而「人們 expect（預期）未來的通膨會是多少」是自然的句構。remember 指的是過去，而 prefer 和 forbid 都不是預測。
zh.Fixed phrase: “in anticipation” means in: 固定用語：in anticipation（預先、預期地）表示在預料的事情發生之前。企業因為預期物價上漲而漲價；其他名詞都無法構成合適的片語。
zh.Economists say expectations are “anchore: 當預期穩定地維持在目標附近時，經濟學家會說預期被 anchored（錨定），這正是設定明確目標的目的。hidden、doubled 或 reversed 的預期都不是目的。
zh.Phrasal verb: “bring inflation back down: 片語動詞：bring inflation back down（讓通膨回落）到目標水準。out、away 和 off 都無法表示降低。

questions.title: Antarctic krill
parts: Antarctic krill are small shrimp-like animals, rarely longer than six centimetres, yet their combined weight may
that of all the humans on Earth. They form the base of the Southern Ocean food
, feeding whales, seals, penguins and fish. Krill depend on algae that grow on the underside of sea ice, so the
of winter ice in some regions is a serious concern. A growing fishery for krill, used in fish feed and supplements, adds further
on the population.
why: “small … yet” sets up a surprisingly large total: their combined weight may exceed that of all humans. The other verbs do not make a comparison of size.
Ecologists call the feeding relationships in an ecosystem the food web. A food bank or food store is something quite different.
Krill depend on algae under the ice, so the concern must be losing that ice. Growth of winter ice would help them.
A fishery removes krill, so it adds pressure on the population. Support and protection are the opposite of what a fishery does.

zh.Antarctic krill are small shrimp-like an: 南極磷蝦是一種外形像蝦的小型動物，體長很少超過六公分，但牠們的總重量可能 ____ 地球上所有人類的總重量。牠們是南冰洋食物 ____ 的基礎，餵養了鯨魚、海豹、企鵝和魚類。磷蝦依賴生長在海冰底面的藻類，所以某些地區冬季海冰的 ____ 是一個嚴重的問題。日益擴大的磷蝦漁業被用於製造魚飼料和營養補充品，對磷蝦族群造成了更多 ____ 。
zh.“small … yet” sets up a surprisingly lar: 「體型很小…但是」鋪陳了一個出乎意料的龐大總量：牠們的總重量可能 exceed（超過）所有人類。其他動詞都無法構成大小的比較。
zh.Ecologists call the feeding relationship: 生態學家把生態系中的攝食關係稱為 food web（食物網）。food bank（食物銀行）或 food store 則是完全不同的東西。
zh.Krill depend on algae under the ice, so: 磷蝦依賴海冰下的藻類，所以令人擔憂的一定是海冰的 loss（消失）。冬季海冰增加反而對牠們有利。
zh.A fishery removes krill, so it adds pres: 漁業會捕撈磷蝦，所以它對族群增加了 pressure（壓力）。support 和 protection 都與漁業的作用相反。

questions.title: Who maintains open-source software?
parts: Much of the software that runs the internet is open source, meaning its code is freely available for anyone to use,
and share. Many projects are maintained by volunteers, sometimes by only one or two people, even though large companies
on them every day. This creates a risk: a small team with no
may struggle to fix security problems quickly. In recent years, some companies and governments have begun to
the maintainers of critical projects, recognising that free software still has costs.
why: Open-source licences let people use, modify and share code. Hiding or deleting it contradicts “freely available”.
Collocation: depend on. The sentence stresses how much large companies rely on volunteer work every day.
The last sentence says free software “still has costs”, so the risk is a team without money: no funding.
Recognising that the software has costs explains why they began to pay the maintainers. Ignoring or criticising them would not meet those costs.

zh.Much of the software that runs the inter: 支撐網際網路運作的軟體中，有很大一部分是開放原始碼軟體，也就是任何人都可以免費使用、____ 和分享其程式碼。許多專案是由志工維護的，有時只有一兩個人，即使大公司每天都 ____ 這些專案。這就造成了一種風險：一個沒有 ____ 的小團隊，可能很難迅速修補安全漏洞。近年來，一些公司和政府開始 ____ 關鍵專案的維護者，因為他們認識到免費軟體仍然有成本。
zh.Open-source licences let people use, mod: 開放原始碼授權讓人們可以使用、modify（修改）和分享程式碼。隱藏或刪除程式碼與「免費提供」相矛盾。
zh.Collocation: depend on. The sentence str: 固定搭配：depend on（依賴）。這句話強調大公司每天有多麼依賴志工的工作。
zh.The last sentence says free software “st: 最後一句說免費軟體「仍然有成本」，所以風險在於團隊沒有錢：no funding（沒有資金）。
zh.Recognising that the software has costs: 認識到軟體有成本，就解釋了他們為什麼開始 pay（支付報酬給）維護者。忽視或批評他們都無法支付這些成本。

questions.title: Do sugar taxes work?
parts: Several countries have introduced taxes on sugary soft drinks to
obesity and tooth decay. Critics predicted that consumers would simply pay the higher price, but the evidence has been more encouraging. In the United Kingdom, the tax was designed to
manufacturers rather than shoppers: drinks with less sugar were taxed at a lower rate or not at all. Many companies
their recipes before the tax began, and the average sugar content of soft drinks fell sharply. The effect on obesity is harder to
, because diet depends on many other foods.
why: A health tax aims to reduce obesity and tooth decay. “cause”, “celebrate” and “advertise” make no sense as the purpose of the tax.
By taxing sugar content, the tax aimed at manufacturers rather than shoppers: it was designed to target them. It does not “reward” them.
The average sugar content fell because companies changed their recipes to avoid the tax. “protected” or “copied” their recipes would not lower the sugar.
“because diet depends on many other foods” explains why the effect is difficult to isolate, so it is harder to measure.

zh.Several countries have introduced taxes: 好幾個國家已經對含糖飲料課稅，以 ____ 肥胖和蛀牙。批評者預測消費者只會乖乖付更高的價錢，但證據卻更令人鼓舞。在英國，這項稅的設計是 ____ 製造商而不是消費者：含糖量較低的飲料稅率較低，甚至完全不課稅。許多公司在稅制開始之前就 ____ 了配方，飲料的平均含糖量也大幅下降。對肥胖的影響則比較難 ____ ，因為飲食還取決於許多其他食物。
zh.A health tax aims to reduce obesity and: 健康稅的目的是 reduce（減少）肥胖和蛀牙。cause、celebrate 和 advertise 作為課稅的目的都說不通。
zh.By taxing sugar content, the tax aimed a: 透過對含糖量課稅，這項稅針對的是製造商而不是消費者：它的設計是 target（針對）製造商，而不是獎勵他們。
zh.The average sugar content fell because c: 平均含糖量下降，是因為公司 changed（改變）了配方以避稅。protected 或 copied 配方都無法降低含糖量。
zh.“because diet depends on many other food: 「因為飲食還取決於許多其他食物」說明了這種影響很難單獨區分出來，所以比較難 measure（測量）。

questions.title: The first writing
parts: The earliest known writing, cuneiform, appeared in Mesopotamia around 3200 BCE. It did not begin as a way to record stories or laws but as a system for
goods such as grain and livestock. Scribes pressed a reed into wet clay to make wedge-shaped marks, and the tablets were then dried in the sun or
in kilns. Over centuries the signs became more abstract and began to
sounds as well as objects, allowing the script to record several different languages. Hundreds of thousands of tablets have
, because baked clay lasts far longer than paper.
why: Early writing was a form of accounting, so it was a system for counting goods such as grain and livestock. Cooking, painting or hiding goods is not what a writing system records.
Kilns are ovens for firing clay, so the tablets were baked. Clay cannot be frozen, washed or folded in a kiln.
Signs that stand for sounds represent them, and that is what allowed several languages to be written.
“because baked clay lasts far longer than paper” explains why so many tablets have survived. “disappeared” contradicts the reason given.

zh.The earliest known writing, cuneiform, a: 已知最早的文字——楔形文字——大約在西元前 3200 年出現於美索不達米亞。它最初並不是用來記錄故事或法律，而是一套用來 ____ 穀物和牲畜等物品的系統。書記員把蘆葦筆壓進濕黏土中，刻出楔形的記號，然後把泥板放在陽光下曬乾，或放進窯中 ____ 。數個世紀以來，這些符號變得越來越抽象，並開始 ____ 聲音和物體，使這種文字能記錄好幾種不同的語言。數十萬片泥板得以 ____ ，因為燒過的黏土比紙張持久得多。
zh.Early writing was a form of accounting,: 早期的文字是一種記帳方式，所以它是一套 counting（計算、點算）穀物和牲畜等物品的系統。烹煮、繪畫或隱藏物品都不是文字系統所記錄的內容。
zh.Kilns are ovens for firing clay, so the: 窯是燒製黏土的爐子，所以泥板被 baked（燒製）。黏土不能在窯中被冷凍、清洗或摺疊。
zh.Signs that stand for sounds represent th: 代表聲音的符號就是在 represent（代表）聲音，這正是讓好幾種語言得以被書寫的原因。
zh.“because baked clay lasts far longer tha: 「因為燒過的黏土比紙張持久得多」解釋了為什麼有這麼多泥板 survived（保存下來）。disappeared 與所給的理由相矛盾。

questions.title: The wisdom of crowds
parts: In 1906, the scientist Francis Galton visited a country fair where visitors guessed the weight of an ox. Individual guesses varied widely, but the
of all the guesses was within one per cent of the true weight. This effect, later called the wisdom of crowds, works only under certain
. The people must judge independently, because if they influence one another, their errors no longer
out. That is why a group discussion can sometimes produce a
estimate than simply averaging private opinions.
why: Combining many guesses into one number means taking their average. The “winner” would be a single person’s guess, not all of them.
“works only under certain conditions” is the standard phrase, and the next sentence goes on to give one condition.
Phrasal verb: errors “cancel out” when high and low guesses balance each other. That is exactly what independence allows.
Discussion makes people influence each other, which destroys independence, so it can produce a worse estimate than averaging private opinions.

zh.In 1906, the scientist Francis Galton vi: 1906 年，科學家法蘭西斯・高爾頓參觀了一個鄉村市集，那裡的遊客在猜一頭牛的重量。個別的猜測差異很大，但所有猜測的 ____ 與實際重量只差不到百分之一。這種後來被稱為「群眾智慧」的效應，只有在特定的 ____ 下才會成立。人們必須獨立做出判斷，因為如果他們互相影響，他們的誤差就不再能互相 ____ 。這就是為什麼小組討論有時會產生比單純平均個人意見更 ____ 的估計。
zh.Combining many guesses into one number m: 把許多猜測合併成一個數字，就是取它們的 average（平均值）。winner 只是一個人的猜測，而不是全部的猜測。
zh.“works only under certain conditions” is: works only under certain conditions（只有在特定條件下才成立）是標準用語，而下一句接著就提出了其中一個條件。
zh.Phrasal verb: errors “cancel out” when h: 片語動詞：當偏高和偏低的猜測彼此抵銷時，誤差就會 cancel out（互相抵消）。這正是獨立判斷所帶來的效果。
zh.Discussion makes people influence each o: 討論會讓人們互相影響，破壞了獨立性，所以它可能產生比平均個人意見更 worse（更差）的估計。

questions.title: Why clocks run clockwise
parts: The direction a clock's hands move was decided long before clocks existed. In the northern hemisphere, the shadow cast by a sundial sweeps from west to north to east as the day
, and the first mechanical clocks were built to
that familiar movement. Had the technology been developed in the southern hemisphere, where shadows run the other way, our clocks would almost certainly turn in the
direction. The convention survived because it had become too widely
to change, which is why a few modern clocks that run backwards are sold as curiosities rather than as improvements.
why: The shadow moves as the day goes on, so the day progresses. “retreats” and “shortens” describe the shadow, not the day.
The first clocks were built to imitate the sundial, that is, to copy its movement. They did not explain or measure the shadow itself.
Shadows run the other way in the southern hemisphere, so clocks made there would turn in the opposite direction.
A convention too widely established is one too entrenched to change. “invented” would not explain why it survived.

zh.The direction a clock's hands move was d: 時鐘指針轉動的方向，早在時鐘出現之前就已經決定了。在北半球，隨著一天 ____ ，日晷投下的影子會由西轉北再轉東，而最早的機械鐘就是為了 ____ 這個熟悉的移動方式而製造的。如果這項技術是在影子走向相反的南半球發展出來的，我們的時鐘幾乎一定會朝 ____ 的方向轉。這個慣例之所以留存下來，是因為它已經被 ____ 得太廣泛而難以改變，這也是為什麼少數逆時針運轉的現代時鐘，是當成新奇玩意兒而不是改良品在販售。
zh.The shadow moves as the day goes on, so: 影子隨著一天的進行而移動，所以是一天 progresses（推進）。retreats 和 shortens 描述的是影子，而不是一天。
zh.The first clocks were built to imitate t: 最早的時鐘是為了模仿日晷而製造，也就是 copy（複製）它的移動方式。它們並不是在解釋或測量影子本身。
zh.Shadows run the other way in the souther: 南半球的影子走向相反，所以在那裡製造的時鐘會朝 opposite（相反）的方向轉。
zh.A convention too widely established is o: 一個被 established（確立）得太廣泛的慣例，就是根深蒂固、難以改變的慣例。invented 無法解釋它為何得以留存。

questions.title: Why the lights go out
parts: An electricity grid has to match supply to demand second by second, because electricity cannot easily be
. If generation falls behind consumption, the frequency of the system drops, and equipment designed for fifty or sixty cycles begins to
. Operators therefore keep a reserve of plant that can be started at short notice, and they will shed load — cutting power to some customers deliberately — rather than allow the whole network to

. A blackout that affects millions is almost never caused by one failure. It is caused by a first failure that shifts power onto neighbouring lines, which then overload in turn, a chain that can spread across a continent in
than a minute.
why: Supply must match demand because electricity cannot easily be stored. It certainly can be produced, measured and exported.
Equipment built for a fixed frequency begins to fail when the frequency drops. “improve” and “cool” do not follow from a falling frequency.
Operators cut power to some customers to stop the whole network collapsing, which is the outcome they are avoiding.
A chain reaction that spreads in under a minute spreads in less than a minute. “more” would make the sentence say the opposite.

zh.An electricity grid has to match supply: 電網必須分秒不差地讓供給與需求相符，因為電力不容易 ____ 。如果發電落後於用電，系統頻率就會下降，而為五十或六十赫茲設計的設備就會開始 ____ 。因此，電力調度員會保留可以在短時間內啟動的備用機組，並且寧可卸載——刻意切斷部分用戶的供電——也不讓整個電網 ____ 。影響數百萬人的大停電幾乎從來不是單一故障造成的。它起因於第一個故障把電力推向鄰近線路，這些線路接著也過載，這條連鎖反應可以在 ____ 一分鐘的時間內蔓延整片大陸。
zh.Supply must match demand because electri: 供給必須與需求相符，是因為電力不容易 stored（儲存）。電力當然可以被生產、測量和輸出。
zh.Equipment built for a fixed frequency be: 為固定頻率設計的設備在頻率下降時會開始 fail（故障）。improve 和 cool 都不是頻率下降的結果。
zh.Operators cut power to some customers to: 調度員切斷部分用戶的供電，是為了避免整個電網 collapse（崩潰），那正是他們要避免的結果。
zh.A chain reaction that spreads in under a: 在不到一分鐘內蔓延的連鎖反應，就是 less than a minute（不到一分鐘）。more 會讓句子變成相反的意思。

questions.title: The trolley that changed shopping
parts: When an Oklahoma grocer introduced the shopping trolley in 1937, nobody used it. Men thought pushing a cart looked
, and women said it reminded them of a pram. The owner hired actors to wheel trolleys around his store looking perfectly at

, and within a year the invention had spread. Its effect on retailing was larger than its inventor expected: a customer who can carry only an armful buys an armful, so the size of the basket ultimately
what a shop can sell. Trolleys have grown steadily larger ever since, and studies find that doubling the capacity raises spending by roughly a
, even when the shopping list has not changed.
why: The objection was about appearance: men thought pushing a cart made them look weak. “expensive” and “modern” are not reasons to refuse.
To look “perfectly at ease” is to look relaxed, which is how the hired actors made the trolley seem normal.
The sentence explains that a customer carrying an armful buys an armful, so basket size limits sales.
A proportion is needed, and “roughly a fifth” fits with “raises spending by”. “a hundred” and “a dozen” are not proportions.

zh.When an Oklahoma grocer introduced the s: 一九三七年，奧克拉荷馬州一位雜貨商引進購物推車時，沒有人願意使用。男人覺得推著車子看起來很 ____ ，女人則說那讓她們想起嬰兒車。店主於是僱了演員在店裡推著推車走動，神情十分 ____ ，一年之內這項發明就普及開來。它對零售業的影響比發明者預期得大：只能用雙手抱多少就買多少的顧客，買的就是那麼多，因此購物籃的大小最終 ____ 了一家店能賣出多少。從那時起，推車越做越大，而研究發現，容量加倍會讓消費額提高約 ____ ，即使購物清單並沒有改變。
zh.The objection was about appearance: men: 反對的理由關乎觀感：男人覺得推車子會讓自己看起來 weak（軟弱）。expensive 和 modern 都不是拒絕的理由。
zh.To look “perfectly at ease” is to look r: look perfectly at ease（神情自若）就是看起來很自在，僱來的演員正是以此讓推車顯得稀鬆平常。
zh.The sentence explains that a customer ca: 這句話說明顧客能抱多少就買多少，因此購物籃的大小 limits（限制）了銷售。
zh.A proportion is needed, and “roughly a f: 這裡需要一個比例，而「roughly a fifth（約五分之一）」才能搭配 raises spending by。a hundred 和 a dozen 都不是比例。

questions.title: Flying in formation
parts: Birds that migrate long distances often fly in a V, and the reason is aerodynamic rather than
. Each beating wing leaves behind a swirl of air that rises just outside the wingtip, and a bird positioned there gains lift it does not have to
itself. Measurements on trained ibises show that the birds adjust their position and even the timing of their wingbeats to stay in that rising air, which is a remarkable feat of
. The lead bird gets no such benefit, so the position is rotated. Geese flying in formation have been found to use up to twenty per cent less energy than a bird flying
why: The sentence contrasts an aerodynamic reason with a social one, which is the usual alternative explanation for flying together.
A bird in rising air gains lift it does not have to generate itself, that is, produce with its own effort.
Adjusting position and wingbeat timing to match another bird is a feat of coordination, not of memory or strength.
The comparison is between formation flight and solo flight, so the saving is against a bird flying alone.

zh.Birds that migrate long distances often: 長距離遷徙的鳥類常排成 V 字形飛行，原因在於空氣動力學，而不是 ____ 。每一次拍動的翅膀都會在翼尖外側留下一股向上旋轉的氣流，而待在那個位置的鳥就能獲得牠不必自己 ____ 的升力。對受訓朱鷺的測量顯示，牠們會調整位置、甚至調整拍翅的時機，以保持在那股上升氣流中，這是相當了不起的 ____ 本領。領頭的鳥得不到這種好處，因此這個位置會輪流擔任。研究發現，排成隊形飛行的雁，耗用的能量比 ____ 飛行的鳥少達兩成。
zh.The sentence contrasts an aerodynamic re: 這句話把空氣動力學上的原因與 social（社會性）的原因對比，後者正是對「一起飛行」最常見的另一種解釋。
zh.A bird in rising air gains lift it does: 位於上升氣流中的鳥獲得了牠不必自己 generate（產生）的升力，也就是不必靠自身力氣製造。
zh.Adjusting position and wingbeat timing t: 調整位置甚至拍翅時機以配合另一隻鳥，是 coordination（協調）的本領，而不是記憶或力量。
zh.The comparison is between formation flig: 這裡比較的是編隊飛行與單獨飛行，所以節省的能量是相對於 alone（獨自）飛行的鳥。

questions.title: How the chilli travelled
parts: Chillies are native to the Americas, and no cuisine in Asia or Africa used them before the sixteenth century. Within a hundred years of their arrival they had become
to the cooking of India, Korea, Hungary and West Africa, which is one of the fastest culinary changes on record. Part of the reason is that chillies grow easily in a wide range of
, so a farmer could plant them without permission or capital. The other part is pharmacological: the compound that makes a chilli hot binds to the same receptor that detects
, which is why the sensation feels like burning, and repeated exposure makes that receptor less
. Cultures that adopted chillies therefore kept raising the dose.
why: Becoming essential to a cuisine is becoming central to it. “unknown” contradicts the sentence.
Chillies spread because they grow easily in many climates, which is what lets a farmer plant them anywhere.
Capsaicin binds to the receptor that detects heat, which explains why the sensation feels like burning.
Repeated exposure dulls the receptor, making it less responsive, which is why eaters raise the dose.

zh.Chillies are native to the Americas, and: 辣椒原產於美洲，十六世紀之前，亞洲與非洲沒有任何菜系使用它。傳入之後不到一百年，它就成為印度、韓國、匈牙利與西非料理中 ____ 的元素，這是有紀錄以來飲食變化最快的例子之一。原因之一是辣椒在各種 ____ 中都容易生長，農民不需要許可或資本就能種。另一個原因屬於藥理：讓辣椒變辣的化合物，會與偵測 ____ 的同一種受體結合，這就是為什麼那種感覺像灼燒；而反覆接觸會讓那個受體變得較不 ____ 。因此，採用辣椒的文化會不斷加重劑量。
zh.Becoming essential to a cuisine is becom: 成為某個菜系不可或缺的元素，就是成為 central（核心）的元素。unknown 與句意相矛盾。
zh.Chillies spread because they grow easily: 辣椒之所以傳播，是因為它在許多 climates（氣候）中都容易生長，農民因此到處都能種。
zh.Capsaicin binds to the receptor that det: 辣椒素會與偵測 heat（熱）的受體結合，這解釋了為什麼那種感覺像灼燒。
zh.Repeated exposure dulls the receptor, ma: 反覆接觸會使受體變得遲鈍，也就是較不 responsive（敏感），這就是為什麼食用者會不斷加重劑量。

questions.title: The first public parks
parts: Until the nineteenth century, the large green spaces of European cities were private, and entry
on knowing someone who owned them. Industrial cities changed the argument. Reformers pointed out that workers had nowhere to walk, and that disease spread fastest where air did not
. Birkenhead Park, opened near Liverpool in 1847, was the first paid for entirely from public funds and open to everybody without
. Its designer separated carriages from pedestrians and hid the boundary with planting, so the park seemed to continue beyond its walls — a trick later
by the designers of Central Park, who visited and took notes.
why: Entry depended on knowing an owner. “relied” would need “relied on knowing”, which is possible, but “depended on” is the collocation the sentence sets up with “entry”.
The health argument was about stagnant air, so disease spread where air did not move.
A park open to everybody without charge is a free park; a warning or a delay makes no sense here.
Central Park's designers visited and copied the trick, that is, they borrowed it.

zh.Until the nineteenth century, the large: 直到十九世紀，歐洲城市裡的大片綠地都是私有的，能否進入 ____ 於你是否認識擁有它們的人。工業城市改變了這個論點。改革者指出，工人無處散步，而在空氣不 ____ 的地方疾病傳播最快。一八四七年在利物浦附近開放的伯肯希德公園，是第一座完全以公款興建、而且所有人都能免 ____ 進入的公園。它的設計者把馬車與行人分道，並以植栽遮掩邊界，使公園看起來彷彿延伸到圍牆之外——這個手法後來被中央公園的設計者 ____ ，他們曾親自造訪並做了筆記。
zh.Entry depended on knowing an owner. “rel: 能否進入 depended on（取決於）是否認識園主。relied 雖然也能接 on，但這句以 entry 起頭，depended on 才是自然的搭配。
zh.The health argument was about stagnant a: 健康方面的論點談的是空氣不流通，所以疾病在空氣不 move（流動）的地方傳播最快。
zh.A park open to everybody without charge: 所有人都能 without charge（免費）進入的公園就是免費公園；warning 或 delay 在這裡說不通。
zh.Central Park's designers visited and cop: 中央公園的設計者造訪之後沿用了這個手法，也就是把它 borrowed（借用）過去。

questions.title: Dinner in orbit
parts: Feeding a crew in orbit is mostly a problem of mass. Every kilogram sent beyond the atmosphere costs thousands of dollars, so food is dried, compressed and rehydrated on
. Growing it instead would cut the launch mass dramatically, and experiments on the space station have produced lettuce, radishes and chillies in trays lit by red and blue
. The difficulty is not light but water, which in weightlessness will not drain through soil and instead forms a film around the roots,
them of air. Engineers have responded with clay pellets and wicks that draw moisture by capillary action. Even so, the crops grown so far supply flavour and morale rather than
why: Dried food is rehydrated when it gets there, that is, on arrival. “departure” reverses the sequence.
Plants in orbit are lit by red and blue lamps; mirrors and screens do not produce light.
Water that surrounds the roots and keeps air out is starving them of air, which is the problem the sentence describes.
Flavour and morale are contrasted with the nutritional point of food, which is calories.

zh.Feeding a crew in orbit is mostly a prob: 在軌道上餵飽組員，主要是質量的問題。每送一公斤到大氣層之外都要花費數千美元，因此食物會先乾燥、壓縮，等 ____ 後再加水復原。改以種植的方式供應能大幅減少發射質量，而太空站上的實驗已在以紅光和藍光 ____ 照射的栽培盤中種出萵苣、蘿蔔和辣椒。困難之處不在光，而在水：在失重環境中，水不會從土壤中排出，反而在根部周圍形成一層水膜， ____ 根部的空氣。工程師以黏土顆粒和利用毛細作用吸水的導水芯來因應。即便如此，目前種出的作物提供的是風味與士氣，而不是 ____ 。
zh.Dried food is rehydrated when it gets th: 乾燥食品是在抵達之後才加水復原，也就是 on arrival（抵達時）。departure 會把順序顛倒。
zh.Plants in orbit are lit by red and blue: 軌道上的植物是以紅光與藍光 lamps（燈）照射；mirrors 和 screens 本身不會發光。
zh.Water that surrounds the roots and keeps: 包住根部、把空氣隔絕在外的水，正是在 starving（剝奪）根部的空氣，這就是句子所描述的問題。
zh.Flavour and morale are contrasted with t: 風味與士氣是用來對比食物在營養上的意義，也就是 calories（熱量）。

questions.title: Hearing nothing
parts: Noise-cancelling headphones work by addition rather than by

. A microphone on the outside of the cup samples the incoming sound, a processor inverts the wave so that its peaks line up with the original's troughs, and the speaker plays that inverted copy. Where the two meet they
, and the listener hears something close to silence. The method works best on steady low sounds such as an engine, because the processor has time to
the next cycle. It works poorly on speech, which changes too quickly, which is why a neighbour's conversation remains
on a plane while the roar of the engines disappears.
why: The headphones add an inverted wave instead of physically blocking sound, which is the contrast the sentence draws.
Two waves whose peaks meet troughs cancel each other, leaving near-silence.
A steady tone lets the processor predict the next cycle; recording or amplifying it would not help.
Because speech cannot be cancelled, a neighbour's conversation stays audible while engine noise disappears.

zh.Noise-cancelling headphones work by addi: 降噪耳機靠的是疊加，而不是 ____ 。耳罩外側的麥克風會取樣傳入的聲音，處理器把聲波反相，使它的波峰對準原聲的波谷，再由喇叭播放這份反相的複本。兩者相遇時會互相 ____ ，聽者聽到的便近乎寂靜。這種方法對引擎聲之類穩定的低頻最有效，因為處理器有時間 ____ 下一個週期。它對語音的效果很差，因為語音變化太快，這就是為什麼在飛機上引擎的轟鳴消失了，鄰座的談話卻依然 ____ 。
zh.The headphones add an inverted wave inst: 耳機是加上一段反相的聲波，而不是實體 blocking（阻隔）聲音，這正是句子所做的對比。
zh.Two waves whose peaks meet troughs cance: 波峰對上波谷的兩道聲波會互相 cancel（抵消），留下近乎寂靜。
zh.A steady tone lets the processor predict: 穩定的音調讓處理器得以 predict（預測）下一個週期；把它錄下來或放大並沒有幫助。
zh.Because speech cannot be cancelled, a ne: 由於語音無法被抵消，鄰座的談話仍然 audible（聽得見），而引擎噪音卻消失了。

questions.title: The metal that was once precious
parts: Aluminium is the most abundant metal in the earth's crust, yet in 1850 it was more

than gold. The reason is chemistry: it never occurs as a pure metal, and separating it from oxygen requires an enormous amount of energy. Napoleon III is said to have served his most important guests on aluminium plates and everyone else on
. Within forty years, an electrolytic process discovered independently in France and the United States had cut the price by a factor of two hundred, and the metal moved from the banquet table to the
shed. Recycling it uses about five per cent of the energy of making it new, which is why a drinks can is one of the few objects genuinely worth
to collect.
why: The contrast with gold is about price, so aluminium was more valuable. “common” would not be surprising.
The joke only works if the second metal is one we think of as grander: guests of lower rank got silver.
The metal moved from luxury to industry, so from the banquet table to the factory shed.
If recycling saves that much energy, it is worth paying to collect the cans.

zh.Aluminium is the most abundant metal in: 鋁是地殼中含量最豐富的金屬，但在一八五○年它卻比黃金更 ____ 。原因在於化學：鋁從不以純金屬的形式存在，而要把它從氧當中分離出來需要極大的能量。據說拿破崙三世用鋁製餐盤招待最重要的賓客，其他人則用 ____ 餐盤。不到四十年，法國與美國各自獨立發現的電解法把價格壓低了兩百倍，這種金屬也從宴席走進了 ____ 的廠房。回收鋁所耗的能量約為新煉的百分之五，這就是為什麼飲料罐是少數真正值得 ____ 回收的物品之一。
zh.The contrast with gold is about price, s: 與黃金的對比在於價格，所以鋁當時更 valuable（珍貴）。common 並不令人意外。
zh.The joke only works if the second metal: 這個趣聞之所以成立，是因為第二種金屬在我們印象中較為尊貴：地位較低的賓客用的是 silver（銀）。
zh.The metal moved from luxury to industry,: 這種金屬從奢侈品走向工業，也就是從宴席走進 factory（工廠）廠房。
zh.If recycling saves that much energy, it: 既然回收能省下這麼多能量，就值得 paying（付錢）去回收這些罐子。

questions.title: The edge of a coin
parts: The ridges around the edge of a coin are a solution to a crime that no longer

. When coins were made of silver and gold, their value came from the metal itself, so shaving a sliver from the rim of each coin that passed through your hands produced a quantity of precious metal and left the coins apparently
. The remedy, introduced at the Royal Mint in the seventeenth century, was to mill a pattern into the edge, so that any coin with a shaved rim was immediately
. Modern coins contain almost no valuable metal, and the ridges survive partly out of habit and partly because they help people distinguish coins by
why: Clipping coins is no longer possible, so it is a crime that no longer exists. “pays” would need a different subject.
The point of shaving the rim was that the coins still looked intact, so nobody noticed.
A milled edge makes a shaved coin immediately obvious, which is how the remedy worked.
Ridges are felt rather than seen, so they help people tell coins apart by touch.

zh.The ridges around the edge of a coin are: 硬幣邊緣的刻紋，是為了防範一種如今已不再 ____ 的犯罪。當硬幣以銀和金鑄造時，它的價值來自金屬本身，因此從每一枚經手的硬幣邊緣削下一小片，就能累積出一定數量的貴金屬，而硬幣看起來仍然 ____ 。十七世紀英國皇家鑄幣廠引入的解方，是在邊緣滾壓出紋路，如此一來任何被削過邊的硬幣都會立刻 ____ 。現代硬幣幾乎不含有價值的金屬，這些刻紋留存下來，一部分出於習慣，一部分則是因為它們幫助人們以 ____ 分辨不同幣值。
zh.Clipping coins is no longer possible, so: 削幣如今已不可能，所以那是一種不再 exists（存在）的犯罪。pays 需要另一種主詞。
zh.The point of shaving the rim was that th: 削邊的重點在於硬幣看起來仍然 intact（完整），所以沒有人察覺。
zh.A milled edge makes a shaved coin immedi: 滾花的邊緣讓被削過的硬幣立刻 obvious（顯眼），這正是這個解方奏效的方式。
zh.Ridges are felt rather than seen, so the: 刻紋是用摸的而不是用看的，所以它幫助人們以 touch（觸覺）分辨硬幣。

questions.title: Ants that plant trees
parts: A surprising number of plants rely on ants to move their seeds. The seed carries a small fatty structure, rich in oils, which ants find irresistible; they carry the whole seed back to the nest, feed the attachment to their larvae and discard the seed itself in a refuse chamber. From the plant's point of view this is nearly
: the seed ends up buried, in soil enriched by ant waste, and beyond the reach of the mice that would otherwise eat it. Botanists estimate that around eleven thousand species of plant depend on this
. Where invasive ants replace native ones, the arrangement quietly
, because the newcomers eat the oil where it lies and never
the seed at all.
why: Buried, fertilised and safe from mice is the best possible outcome for a seed, so the arrangement is nearly ideal.
The sentence refers back to the partnership just described, which is an arrangement.
If the newcomers do not carry seeds, the partnership fails. “spreads” contradicts the sentence.
Invasive ants eat the oil on the spot and never move the seed, which is exactly the service that is lost.

zh.A surprising number of plants rely on an: 相當多的植物仰賴螞蟻搬運種子。種子上帶有一小塊富含油脂的附屬構造，螞蟻無法抗拒；牠們會把整顆種子搬回巢中，把那塊附屬構造餵給幼蟲，再把種子本身丟進廢物室。從植物的角度看，這幾乎是 ____ 的安排：種子最後被埋起來，周圍是螞蟻排泄物滋養的土壤，而且遠離本來會把它吃掉的老鼠。植物學家估計，約有一萬一千種植物依賴這種 ____ 。當外來種螞蟻取代原生種時，這套關係會悄悄 ____ ，因為新來者會就地把油脂吃掉，根本不 ____ 種子。
zh.Buried, fertilised and safe from mice is: 被埋起來、有養分、又躲過老鼠，對種子而言是最好的結果，所以這種安排幾乎 ideal（理想）。
zh.The sentence refers back to the partners: 這句話指的是前面描述的那種合作關係，也就是 arrangement（安排）。
zh.If the newcomers do not carry seeds, the: 如果新來者不搬運種子，這套關係就會 fails（失效）。spreads 與句意矛盾。
zh.Invasive ants eat the oil on the spot an: 外來螞蟻就地吃掉油脂，從不 move（搬運）種子，而那正是失去的那項服務。

questions.title: Tuning to A
parts: Before a concert begins, the oboe plays a single note and the orchestra tunes to it. The oboe is chosen because its pitch is the most
of the instruments on stage: it has no slide and little room for adjustment, so everyone else moves to meet it. The note itself, the A above middle C, has not always meant the same
. In the eighteenth century it varied from town to town, and surviving organs show a spread of nearly a whole tone, which is why early music ensembles must decide which century they are playing
. An international conference fixed it at 440 vibrations a second in 1939, although many orchestras now tune slightly
, believing it gives a brighter sound.
why: The oboe leads because its pitch cannot easily be altered, that is, it is the most stable.
The A has not always meant the same frequency, which is what a pitch is measured in.
“which century they are playing in” is the natural phrase; the others do not fit the idiom.
Orchestras tune above 440 for a brighter sound, so slightly higher.

zh.Before a concert begins, the oboe plays: 音樂會開始前，雙簧管會吹出一個音，整個樂團隨之調音。之所以選雙簧管，是因為它的音高是台上樂器中最 ____ 的：它沒有滑管，可調整的空間也很小，所以其他人都得來遷就它。這個音本身——中央 C 上方的 A——也並非一直代表相同的 ____ 。在十八世紀，它因城鎮而異，留存至今的管風琴顯示其差距將近一個全音，這就是為什麼古樂團必須先決定，自己要以 ____ 哪一個世紀的音高來演奏。一九三九年一場國際會議把它定為每秒 440 次振動，不過許多樂團現在會調得略 ____ ，認為這樣音色更明亮。
zh.The oboe leads because its pitch cannot: 由雙簧管起音，是因為它的音高不易改變，也就是最 stable（穩定）。
zh.The A has not always meant the same freq: A 這個音並非一直代表相同的 frequency（頻率），而音高正是以頻率衡量的。
zh.“which century they are playing in” is t: which century they are playing in 是自然的說法；其他選項不合慣用語。
zh.Orchestras tune above 440 for a brighter: 樂團調得高於 440 以求音色明亮，所以是略 higher（高）。

questions.title: How soap works
parts: A soap molecule has two ends that want different things. One end is attracted to water; the other is repelled by it and attracted to oil. Dropped into greasy water, the molecules arrange themselves into tiny spheres with their water-hating ends tucked
, surrounding the grease and holding it in suspension so that it can be rinsed

. This is why washing with water alone fails on anything oily. The same structure explains soap's effect on many viruses, whose outer coat is a fatty membrane: the oil-seeking ends slide into that membrane and
it apart. Twenty seconds of washing is recommended not because the chemistry is slow but because the mechanical
matters as much as the soap.
why: The water-hating ends face in, away from the water, so they are tucked inside the sphere.
Grease held in suspension can be rinsed away, which is the point of the sphere.
The oil-seeking ends get into the membrane and prise it apart, destroying the virus.
Twenty seconds is about the mechanical action, which is the scrubbing rather than the chemistry.

zh.A soap molecule has two ends that want d: 肥皂分子有兩端，各自想要不同的東西。一端被水吸引，另一端排斥水而被油吸引。落入含油的水中時，這些分子會排成微小的球體，把怕水的那一端收在 ____ ，包住油脂並讓它懸浮，好讓它能被沖 ____ 。這就是為什麼只用清水洗不掉油膩的東西。同樣的結構也解釋了肥皂對許多病毒的作用，因為這些病毒的外套膜是脂質的：親油的那一端會滑進膜中，把它 ____ 開來。建議洗二十秒，並不是因為化學作用慢，而是因為機械性的 ____ 和肥皂一樣重要。
zh.The water-hating ends face in, away from: 怕水的那一端朝內、遠離水，所以是收在球體 inside（內部）。
zh.Grease held in suspension can be rinsed: 被懸浮住的油脂可以被沖 away（走），這正是形成球體的目的。
zh.The oil-seeking ends get into the membra: 親油的那一端進入膜中並把它 prise（撬）開，使病毒瓦解。
zh.Twenty seconds is about the mechanical a: 二十秒講的是機械性的動作，也就是 scrubbing（搓洗），而不是化學作用。

questions.title: Machines that translate
parts: For fifty years, machine translation worked by rules: a grammar of the source language, a grammar of the target, and a dictionary between them. The results were poor, because language is full of exceptions that no rulebook
. The breakthrough came from abandoning the attempt to understand and instead feeding systems enormous quantities of text already translated by
, from which statistical patterns could be extracted. Modern systems go further, representing words as positions in a space where related meanings sit

together. The remaining weaknesses are revealing: the systems handle common sentences beautifully and fail on rare ones, they inherit whatever bias the training text contained, and they cannot tell you when they are
why: Exceptions defeat rules because no rulebook anticipates them all.
The statistical approach learns from text already translated by people, which is the data it needs.
Related meanings sit close together in the space, which is what makes the representation useful.
The weakness being described is that a system gives no warning when it is wrong.

zh.For fifty years, machine translation wor: 機器翻譯有五十年是靠規則運作的：來源語言的文法、目標語言的文法，以及兩者之間的辭典。成果很差，因為語言充滿了任何規則手冊都無法 ____ 的例外。突破來自於放棄「理解」這件事，改為餵給系統大量已由 ____ 翻譯過的文本，再從中萃取統計規律。現代系統更進一步，把詞語表示為某個空間中的位置，讓意義相近的詞彼此靠得很 ____ 。目前仍存在的弱點很能說明問題：這些系統處理常見句子極為出色，遇到罕見句子就失敗；它們會沿襲訓練文本中的任何偏見；而且當它們 ____ 時，無法告訴你。
zh.Exceptions defeat rules because no ruleb: 例外之所以擊敗規則，是因為沒有任何規則手冊能 anticipates（預先設想）得完。
zh.The statistical approach learns from tex: 統計方法學習的是已由 people（人）翻譯過的文本，那正是它需要的資料。
zh.Related meanings sit close together in t: 意義相近的詞在空間中彼此 close（接近），這正是這種表示法有用的原因。
zh.The weakness being described is that a s: 這裡描述的弱點是：系統出 wrong（錯）時不會發出任何警告。

questions.passage: Artificial light at night has increased by roughly two per cent a year worldwide over the past decade, and satellite measurements probably understate the change, because the sensors cannot detect the blue-rich light emitted by modern LEDs. The ecological effects are better documented than many people assume. Migrating birds that navigate by the stars are drawn towards illuminated buildings, where large numbers die in collisions. Sea turtle hatchlings, which instinctively move towards the brighter horizon over the sea, crawl inland towards street lights instead. Insects are affected on a vast scale: a single street lamp can attract and exhaust moths from a wide area, disrupting the pollination of night-flowering plants. The effects on people are less certain. Exposure to light at night suppresses melatonin, a hormone involved in sleep, and some studies link bright outdoor lighting with poorer sleep, but it is difficult to separate lighting from other features of urban life such as noise. Unlike many environmental problems, however, light pollution can be reversed almost instantly. Shielding lamps so that they point downwards, reducing their brightness late at night and choosing warmer colours can cut the impact dramatically without leaving streets unsafe.
questions.q: Which of the following are stated or implied in the passage?
o: Satellite data may underestimate the growth of artificial light.
Sea turtle hatchlings can be misled by lights on land.
Bright outdoor lighting has been proven to cause poor sleep in humans.
Light pollution can be reduced quickly without making streets unsafe.
LED lighting has reduced the ecological impact of street lamps.
why: Correct. “satellite measurements probably understate the change, because the sensors cannot detect the blue-rich light emitted by modern LEDs.”
Correct. Hatchlings “instinctively move towards the brighter horizon over the sea” but “crawl inland towards street lights instead”.
Wrong. The passage says “The effects on people are less certain” and that “it is difficult to separate lighting from other features of urban life”. A link is not proof.
Correct. Light pollution “can be reversed almost instantly”, and the fixes cut the impact “without leaving streets unsafe”.
Wrong. Nothing says LEDs reduced the impact. The only mention of LEDs is that satellites cannot detect their blue-rich light.

zh.Artificial light at night has increased: 過去十年來，全世界夜間的人造光每年增加約百分之二，而衛星測量可能低估了這個變化，因為感測器無法偵測現代 LED 燈所發出的富含藍光的光線。它對生態的影響，比許多人以為的有更充分的紀錄。靠星星導航的遷徙鳥類會被燈火通明的建築物吸引，大量的鳥因撞擊而死亡。剛孵化的小海龜本能地朝海面上較亮的地平線移動，卻反而朝內陸的路燈爬去。昆蟲受到的影響規模更是龐大：一盞路燈就能把廣大範圍內的飛蛾吸引過來並使其精疲力竭，干擾夜間開花植物的授粉。對人類的影響則比較不確定。夜間照光會抑制褪黑激素這種與睡眠有關的荷爾蒙，也有一些研究把明亮的戶外照明與較差的睡眠連結在一起，但很難把照明與噪音等都市生活的其他特徵區分開來。然而，與許多環境問題不同的是，光害幾乎可以立即逆轉。為燈具加上遮罩使其朝下照射、在深夜調降亮度，以及選擇較暖的色溫，都能大幅降低影響，而不會讓街道變得不安全。
zh.Which of the following are stated or imp: 下列哪些是文章中陳述或暗示的內容？
zh.Satellite data may underestimate the gro: 衛星數據可能低估了人造光的增長。
zh.Sea turtle hatchlings can be misled by l: 剛孵化的小海龜可能被陸地上的燈光誤導。
zh.Bright outdoor lighting has been proven: 已經證實明亮的戶外照明會導致人類睡眠品質不佳。
zh.Light pollution can be reduced quickly w: 光害可以迅速減少，而不會讓街道變得不安全。
zh.LED lighting has reduced the ecological: LED 照明已經降低了路燈對生態的影響。
zh.Correct. “satellite measurements probabl: 正確。"satellite measurements probably understate the change, because the sensors cannot detect the blue-rich light emitted by modern LEDs."
zh.Correct. Hatchlings “instinctively move: 正確。小海龜 "instinctively move towards the brighter horizon over the sea"，但卻 "crawl inland towards street lights instead"。
zh.Wrong. The passage says “The effects on: 錯誤。文章說 "The effects on people are less certain"，而且 "it is difficult to separate lighting from other features of urban life"。有關聯並不等於有證據。
zh.Correct. Light pollution “can be reverse: 正確。光害 "can be reversed almost instantly"，而這些改善方法能降低影響 "without leaving streets unsafe"。
zh.Wrong. Nothing says LEDs reduced the imp: 錯誤。文章沒有說 LED 降低了影響。唯一提到 LED 的地方，是衛星無法偵測它們富含藍光的光線。

questions.passage: The two-day weekend is a surprisingly recent invention. For most of history, working people had at most one day of rest, usually determined by religion: Sunday for Christians, Saturday for Jews and Friday for Muslims. In nineteenth-century Britain, many factory workers informally extended their rest by taking Monday off, a custom known as Saint Monday, which employers found impossible to stamp out. Some manufacturers eventually offered a compromise: a half-day on Saturday in exchange for reliable attendance on Monday. The full two-day weekend spread in the twentieth century. In the United States, the carmaker Henry Ford introduced a five-day week in 1926, arguing that workers with more leisure time would buy more consumer goods, including cars. During the Great Depression, shorter weeks were also promoted as a way of sharing limited work among more people. By the 1940s the Saturday–Sunday weekend was standard in much of the industrialised world. Today some economists predict that the same pressures, rising productivity and changing ideas about leisure, could eventually produce a three-day weekend, although so far trials have been confined to a small number of companies.
questions.q: Which of the following statements are supported by the passage?
o: Before the modern weekend, the day of rest depended largely on religion.
Saturday half-days were partly a response to workers taking Mondays off.
Henry Ford introduced the five-day week mainly to reduce accidents in his factories.
Shorter working weeks were seen as a way to spread work during the Depression.
A three-day weekend has already become standard in several industrialised countries.
why: Correct. The one day of rest was “usually determined by religion: Sunday for Christians, Saturday for Jews and Friday for Muslims.”
Correct. Employers offered “a half-day on Saturday in exchange for reliable attendance on Monday”, because workers were taking Mondays off.
Wrong. Ford argued “that workers with more leisure time would buy more consumer goods, including cars.” Accidents are never mentioned.
Correct. “shorter weeks were also promoted as a way of sharing limited work among more people.”
Wrong. “so far trials have been confined to a small number of companies.” A prediction is not a present fact.

zh.The two-day weekend is a surprisingly re: 兩天的週末其實是相當晚近才出現的。在歷史的大部分時間裡，勞動者最多只有一天休息日，而且通常由宗教決定：基督徒是星期日，猶太人是星期六，穆斯林則是星期五。在十九世紀的英國，許多工廠工人會非正式地在星期一休假來延長休息時間，這種習俗被稱為「聖星期一」，雇主們發現根本無法杜絕。一些製造商最後提出了折衷方案：星期六放半天假，交換條件是星期一要確實出勤。完整的兩天週末在二十世紀普及開來。在美國，汽車製造商亨利・福特於 1926 年實施每週五天工作制，他主張擁有更多休閒時間的工人會購買更多消費品，包括汽車。在經濟大蕭條期間，縮短工時也被推廣為讓更多人分攤有限工作的一種方法。到了 1940 年代，星期六和星期日的週末已成為工業化世界大部分地區的標準。如今，一些經濟學家預測，同樣的壓力——生產力提高以及對休閒觀念的改變——最終可能會帶來三天的週末，不過到目前為止，試行只限於少數幾家公司。
zh.Which of the following statements are su: 下列哪些敘述有文章內容的支持？
zh.Before the modern weekend, the day of re: 在現代週末出現之前，休息日大多取決於宗教。
zh.Saturday half-days were partly a respons: 星期六放半天假，部分是為了回應工人在星期一休假的情況。
zh.Henry Ford introduced the five-day week: 亨利・福特實施每週五天工作制，主要是為了減少工廠裡的意外。
zh.Shorter working weeks were seen as a way: 縮短工時被視為在大蕭條期間分攤工作的一種方式。
zh.A three-day weekend has already become s: 三天的週末已經在好幾個工業化國家成為標準。
zh.Correct. The one day of rest was “usuall: 正確。一天的休息日 "usually determined by religion: Sunday for Christians, Saturday for Jews and Friday for Muslims."
zh.Correct. Employers offered “a half-day o: 正確。雇主提供 "a half-day on Saturday in exchange for reliable attendance on Monday"，因為工人會在星期一休假。
zh.Wrong. Ford argued “that workers with mo: 錯誤。福特主張 "that workers with more leisure time would buy more consumer goods, including cars." 文章從未提到意外。
zh.Correct. “shorter weeks were also promot: 正確。"shorter weeks were also promoted as a way of sharing limited work among more people."
zh.Wrong. “so far trials have been confined: 錯誤。"so far trials have been confined to a small number of companies." 預測並不是現在的事實。

questions.passage: Yawning is one of the most familiar human behaviours, yet its purpose remains disputed. The popular explanation, that we yawn to take in more oxygen, has not survived testing: people breathing air with extra oxygen yawn just as often, and those breathing air with extra carbon dioxide do not yawn more. A more promising idea is that yawning helps to cool the brain. Yawns are more frequent when the brain is warm, and one study found that people holding a cold pack against their forehead yawned less when watching videos of others yawning. Yawning is also contagious, at least among humans, chimpanzees and some dogs. Contagious yawning appears in children only at around the age of four or five, roughly when they begin to understand other people’s mental states, and some studies suggest it is more common between friends and relatives than between strangers. This has led researchers to link it with empathy, although the evidence is mixed, and some larger studies have found that age explains the variation better than empathy does.
questions.q: Which of the following can be concluded from the passage?
o: Experiments do not support the idea that yawning increases oxygen intake.
Cooling the forehead appears to reduce yawning.
Contagious yawning is found only in humans.
Newborn babies already yawn when they see others yawn.
The link between contagious yawning and empathy is not firmly established.
why: Correct. The oxygen explanation “has not survived testing”: extra oxygen does not reduce yawning, and extra carbon dioxide does not increase it.
Correct. People “holding a cold pack against their forehead yawned less when watching videos of others yawning.”
Wrong. Contagious yawning occurs “at least among humans, chimpanzees and some dogs.”
Wrong. Contagious yawning “appears in children only at around the age of four or five.”
Correct. “the evidence is mixed, and some larger studies have found that age explains the variation better than empathy does.”

zh.Yawning is one of the most familiar huma: 打哈欠是人類最熟悉的行為之一，但它的目的至今仍有爭議。一般流行的解釋是我們打哈欠是為了吸入更多氧氣，但這個說法經不起檢驗：呼吸含氧量較高空氣的人，打哈欠的次數並沒有減少，而呼吸二氧化碳較多空氣的人，打哈欠的次數也沒有增加。一個較有希望的說法是，打哈欠有助於為大腦降溫。大腦溫度較高時，打哈欠的頻率較高，而一項研究發現，把冰敷袋貼在額頭上的人，在觀看別人打哈欠的影片時，打哈欠的次數較少。打哈欠也會傳染，至少在人類、黑猩猩和某些狗身上是如此。傳染性的打哈欠在兒童約四、五歲時才會出現，大約是他們開始理解他人心理狀態的時候，而且有些研究顯示，它在朋友和親人之間比在陌生人之間更常見。這使研究人員把它與同理心連結起來，不過證據並不一致，一些規模較大的研究發現，年齡比同理心更能解釋其中的差異。
zh.Which of the following can be concluded: 從文章中可以得出下列哪些結論？
zh.Experiments do not support the idea that: 實驗並不支持打哈欠能增加氧氣攝取量的說法。
zh.Cooling the forehead appears to reduce y: 讓額頭降溫似乎能減少打哈欠。
zh.Contagious yawning is found only in huma: 傳染性的打哈欠只存在於人類身上。
zh.Newborn babies already yawn when they se: 新生兒看到別人打哈欠時就已經會跟著打哈欠。

questions.passage: Dogs were the first animals to be domesticated, but when and where it happened remains contested. Genetic studies suggest that dogs descend from a population of wolves that has since become extinct, rather than from the grey wolves alive today. Estimates of the timing range from about fifteen thousand to more than thirty thousand years ago, well before the beginning of farming. This timing matters, because it means dogs were domesticated by hunter-gatherers rather than settled farmers. One popular theory suggests that the process began without deliberate human effort. Wolves that were less fearful of people may have scavenged near human camps, gaining access to food scraps, and over many generations these bolder animals became increasingly tolerant of humans. People may later have valued them for hunting and as guards. Some researchers have also suggested that dogs were domesticated more than once, in both Europe and East Asia, although this remains a minority view. What is widely accepted is that the relationship shaped both species: dogs evolved the ability to digest starch, a change that tracks the spread of human agriculture.
questions.q: Which of the following are stated in the passage?
o: Dogs were domesticated before humans began farming.
Modern grey wolves are the direct ancestors of dogs.
Domestication may have begun with wolves scavenging near human camps.
Most researchers agree that dogs were domesticated twice.
Dogs developed the ability to digest starch.
why: Correct. The timing is “well before the beginning of farming”, so dogs “were domesticated by hunter-gatherers rather than settled farmers”.
Wrong. Dogs descend from “a population of wolves that has since become extinct, rather than from the grey wolves alive today”.
Correct. “Wolves that were less fearful of people may have scavenged near human camps, gaining access to food scraps.”
Wrong. Two domestications is described as “a minority view”, the opposite of what most researchers think.
Correct. “dogs evolved the ability to digest starch, a change that tracks the spread of human agriculture.”

questions.passage: Cities are usually thought of as hostile to wildlife, yet a surprising number of species thrive in them. Peregrine falcons nest on skyscrapers, which resemble the cliffs they use in the wild, and feed on the plentiful city pigeons. Some urban areas even contain more plant species than the surrounding countryside, partly because gardens and parks include many non-native plants and partly because intensive farming has reduced diversity in rural areas. However, species richness can be misleading. Cities tend to favour adaptable generalists, such as foxes, crows and rats, while specialists that depend on particular habitats disappear. As a result, urban wildlife around the world is becoming increasingly similar, a process ecologists call biotic homogenisation. There are also costs for the animals that succeed. Urban birds often sing at a higher pitch to be heard above traffic, and artificial light at night can disrupt their breeding cycles. Planners are increasingly trying to support urban wildlife through green roofs, wildlife corridors connecting parks, and the reduction of unnecessary lighting.
questions.q: Which of the following can be concluded from the passage?
o: Some cities have more plant species than nearby rural areas.
Cities benefit specialist species more than generalists.
Urban wildlife in different cities is becoming more alike.
Peregrine falcons avoid cities because they lack cliffs.
City life can impose costs even on species that do well there.
why: Correct. “Some urban areas even contain more plant species than the surrounding countryside.”
Wrong. The reverse: cities “favour adaptable generalists”, while specialists “disappear”.
Correct. “urban wildlife around the world is becoming increasingly similar”, which is called biotic homogenisation.
Wrong. Falcons nest on skyscrapers, “which resemble the cliffs they use in the wild”.
Correct. “There are also costs for the animals that succeed”, such as higher-pitched song and disrupted breeding.

questions.passage: Public fear of nuclear power is closely linked to a small number of dramatic accidents, especially Chernobyl in 1986 and Fukushima in 2011. Yet when researchers compare energy sources by the number of deaths per unit of electricity produced, including accidents and air pollution, nuclear power ranks among the safest, alongside wind and solar. Coal is by far the most dangerous, mainly because the pollution from burning it contributes to heart and lung disease. At Fukushima, the radiation itself is thought to have caused very few deaths; most of the lives lost were connected to the stress and disruption of a rushed evacuation, particularly among elderly people. None of this means nuclear power is free of problems. Plants are expensive and slow to build, and the long-term storage of radioactive waste remains politically difficult in most countries. But researchers argue that decisions about energy should be based on the full comparison of risks, rather than on the vividness of rare disasters.
questions.q: Which statements are supported by the passage?
o: Measured by deaths per unit of electricity, nuclear power is among the safest sources.
Coal is the most dangerous source mainly because of mining accidents.
Most deaths linked to Fukushima were related to the evacuation rather than radiation.
Nuclear plants are cheap and quick to build.
Radioactive waste storage has been fully solved in most countries.
why: Correct. By deaths per unit of electricity, “nuclear power ranks among the safest, alongside wind and solar”.
Wrong. Coal is most dangerous “mainly because the pollution from burning it contributes to heart and lung disease”, not because of mining accidents.
Correct. “most of the lives lost were connected to the stress and disruption of a rushed evacuation”.
Wrong. “Plants are expensive and slow to build.”
Wrong. Waste storage “remains politically difficult in most countries”.

questions.passage: Kelp forests are underwater forests of large brown algae that grow in cool, nutrient-rich coastal waters. Some kelp species can grow up to half a metre in a single day, making them among the fastest-growing organisms on Earth. The forests provide food and shelter for hundreds of species, from fish to sea otters. Sea otters in turn protect the kelp by eating sea urchins, which would otherwise graze the forests down to bare rock. When otters were hunted almost to extinction for their fur, urchin populations exploded along parts of the Pacific coast, and large areas of kelp disappeared. More recently, marine heatwaves have caused dramatic losses, since kelp struggles in warm water. Restoration projects are now removing urchins by hand and replanting kelp, with some success. Kelp is also attracting commercial interest as a food, a fertiliser and a possible way of storing carbon, although how much of that carbon is stored permanently is still debated.
questions.q: Which of the following are stated or implied in the passage?
o: Sea otters damage kelp forests by feeding on them.
The decline of sea otters led to kelp losses in some areas.
Marine heatwaves have harmed kelp forests.
Scientists agree that kelp stores large amounts of carbon permanently.
why: Correct. Some species “can grow up to half a metre in a single day”.
Wrong. Otters “protect the kelp by eating sea urchins”; it is the urchins that graze the forests.
Correct. When otters were hunted, “urchin populations exploded … and large areas of kelp disappeared”.
Correct. “marine heatwaves have caused dramatic losses, since kelp struggles in warm water”.
Wrong. “how much of that carbon is stored permanently is still debated”.

questions.passage: The fork is such an ordinary object that it is easy to forget how recently it became common. Although small forks were used in the ancient world for serving food, eating with a personal fork spread into Europe from the Byzantine Empire only around the eleventh century. Early reactions were often hostile. Church leaders criticised the fork as an unnecessary luxury, arguing that fingers were good enough for the food God had provided. For several centuries, Europeans continued to eat mainly with knives, spoons and their hands, and the fork was associated with the Italian upper classes. It became common in England only in the eighteenth century, and early forks had just two straight prongs, which were better for holding meat steady while cutting than for lifting food. The curved, four-pronged fork familiar today developed later, as eating habits changed. In much of East Asia, meanwhile, chopsticks had been in everyday use for well over two thousand years.
questions.q: Which of the following are stated in the passage?
o: Personal forks reached Europe from the Byzantine Empire.
Church leaders encouraged forks as a sign of good manners.
Forks became common in England in the eighteenth century.
Early forks usually had four curved prongs.
Chopsticks were in use in East Asia long before forks were common in Europe.
why: Correct. Eating with a personal fork “spread into Europe from the Byzantine Empire only around the eleventh century”.
Wrong. Church leaders “criticised the fork as an unnecessary luxury”.
Correct. “It became common in England only in the eighteenth century.”
Wrong. “early forks had just two straight prongs”; the curved, four-pronged fork “developed later”.
Correct. Chopsticks “had been in everyday use for well over two thousand years”.

questions.passage: Gamification, the use of game features such as points, badges and leaderboards in non-game settings, has become popular in education. Supporters argue that it makes learning more engaging, particularly for students who struggle with motivation. Research gives a mixed picture. Many studies report short-term increases in participation, especially when students receive frequent feedback on their progress. However, these gains often fade once the novelty wears off, and some studies find that leaderboards discourage lower-performing students, who see themselves permanently near the bottom. Psychologists also warn that external rewards can weaken interest in an activity that students already enjoy, a phenomenon known as the overjustification effect. The most successful designs appear to be those that use game elements to support learning goals rather than replace them, for example by giving students clear, achievable challenges and letting them see their own improvement over time rather than comparing them with classmates.
questions.q: Which of the following are supported by the passage?
o: Gamification often increases participation in the short term.
The benefits of gamification usually grow stronger over time.
Leaderboards can discourage students who rank low.
External rewards can reduce interest in activities students already enjoy.
The best designs compare each student’s progress with that of their classmates.
why: Correct. “Many studies report short-term increases in participation.”
Wrong. “these gains often fade once the novelty wears off”.
Correct. “leaderboards discourage lower-performing students, who see themselves permanently near the bottom”.
Correct. “external rewards can weaken interest in an activity that students already enjoy”, the overjustification effect.
Wrong. The best designs let students see “their own improvement over time rather than comparing them with classmates”.

questions.passage: Historians and scientists have increasingly identified the year 536 as one of the worst times to be alive in recorded history. Writers in Europe and the Middle East described a mysterious fog that dimmed the sun for more than a year, and summer temperatures in parts of the northern hemisphere fell sharply. Tree rings from this period show some of the slowest growth ever recorded, and chronicles report failed harvests and famine in regions as far apart as Ireland and China. For a long time the cause was unknown. Analysis of ice cores from Greenland and Antarctica has now revealed evidence of a major volcanic eruption early in 536, followed by further eruptions in 540 and 547, which together kept temperatures low for over a decade. Some researchers link the resulting hardship to the spread of plague a few years later, arguing that populations weakened by hunger were more vulnerable, although that connection remains difficult to prove.

Wrong. There were further eruptions “in 540 and 547, which together kept temperatures low”.
Wrong. That connection “remains difficult to prove”.

questions.passage:
Until the middle of the nineteenth century, every screw was made by hand and fitted only the hole it was cut for. A nut from one workshop would not turn on a bolt from another, and a machine that broke in a distant town could not be repaired without a smith to make a new fastening from scratch. Joseph Whitworth collected samples from across Britain, measured them, and in 1841 proposed a single thread form with a fixed angle and a defined number of turns per inch. Adoption was slow and driven mostly by the railways, which operated across regions and could not tolerate parts that fitted only locally.

The British standard was not the one that won. American manufacturers adopted a different thread, and after 1945 an international system based on millimetres gradually displaced both, although the older threads survive in plumbing and in restored machinery. What matters historically is less which standard prevailed than that one did. Interchangeable fastenings made it possible to manufacture a component in one country, ship it, and have it fit — the precondition for every assembly line that followed.

Standards of this kind are easy to overlook because their success makes them invisible. They are also costly to change: a country that adopts a new thread must retool its factories and keep both systems running for decades, which is why the United States still measures its screws in fractions of an inch.
questions.q: Which of the following are stated in the passage?
o: Before standardisation, a nut from one workshop would not fit a bolt from another.

The railways were the main force behind early adoption.

Changing a national standard is expensive because factories must be retooled.
why: Stated in the opening: parts fitted only the hole they were cut for.
The passage says the British standard was not the one that won; an American thread and later a metric system displaced it.
Stated: adoption was slow and driven mostly by the railways.
The passage says older threads survive in plumbing and restored machinery.
Stated in the final paragraph: a country adopting a new thread must retool and run both systems for decades.

zh.Until the middle of the nineteenth centu: 直到十九世紀中葉，每一顆螺絲都是手工製造的，而且只配得上它所切削的那個孔。某間工坊的螺帽無法鎖上另一間工坊的螺栓，而在遠方城鎮壞掉的機器，若沒有鐵匠從頭打造新的扣件就修不好。約瑟夫・惠特沃斯蒐集了全英國的樣本加以測量，並在一八四一年提出單一的螺紋規格，固定了牙角與每英吋的牙數。推行的速度很慢，主要是由鐵路業帶動的，因為鐵路跨越區域營運，無法忍受只能在地使用的零件。
zh.The British standard was not the one tha: 最後勝出的並不是英國標準。美國製造商採用了不同的螺紋，而一九四五年之後，以公釐為基礎的國際系統逐漸取代了兩者，不過舊螺紋仍留存在水管工程與修復的老機器中。從歷史上看，重要的不是哪一套標準勝出，而是終於有一套標準出現。可互換的扣件讓人們得以在一個國家製造零件、運送出去，並且裝得上——這正是後來每一條裝配線的前提。

questions.passage:
A beaver dam is not built to create a pond. Beavers dam running water because the sound of it signals a gap in their defences; the pond is a by-product, and a beaver will dam a loudspeaker playing a recording of a stream. The consequences for a landscape are nevertheless profound. A single family can flood several hectares, kill the standing trees, and convert a fast channel into a chain of pools, wet meadow and dead wood.

For most of the twentieth century this was regarded as damage. Beavers were trapped out of most of their range in Europe and North America, and the wetlands they had maintained for thousands of years drained and dried. Reassessment began when hydrologists measured what the ponds actually do. They hold water through a drought, release it slowly, trap sediment and nitrogen that would otherwise reach rivers, and raise the water table across a valley floor. Fish populations above beaver dams are generally higher, not lower, because the pools provide cover and cooler water, although the dams do obstruct some migratory species.

Reintroduction is now official policy in several countries, and it has not been uncomplicated. Beavers flood roads and farmland without regard to ownership, and the standard response — a pipe through the dam that lowers the pond without alerting the animals to a leak — needs maintaining. The usual finding is that conflict concentrates in a small number of sites, which is cheaper to manage than it is to argue about.
questions.q: Which of the following are stated in the passage?
o: Beavers dam water in response to the sound of it flowing.
Beaver ponds release water slowly and hold it through droughts.

why: Stated: the sound of running water signals a gap, and beavers will dam a loudspeaker playing a stream.
Stated: the ponds hold water through a drought and release it slowly.
The passage says fish populations above dams are generally higher, not lower.
Stated: beavers were trapped out of most of their range in Europe and North America.
The passage says conflict concentrates in a small number of sites.

zh.A beaver dam is not built to create a po: 河狸築壩並不是為了造出池塘。河狸之所以攔住流水，是因為流水的聲音代表防線有缺口；池塘只是副產品，而河狸甚至會去堵住一個播放溪流錄音的擴音器。然而，這對地景的影響十分深遠。單單一個河狸家族就可能淹沒數公頃土地、淹死站立的樹木，並把湍急的水道變成一連串的水塘、濕草地與枯木。
zh.For most of the twentieth century this w: 在二十世紀的大部分時間裡，這被視為破壞。河狸在歐洲與北美的大部分分布區被捕盡，牠們維持了數千年的濕地也隨之排乾、變得乾燥。重新評價始於水文學家實際測量這些池塘的作用。它們在乾旱中蓄水、緩慢釋放，攔截原本會流入河川的泥沙與氮，並提高整個谷底的地下水位。河狸壩上游的魚群數量通常較高而不是較低，因為水塘提供了遮蔽與較涼的水，儘管這些壩確實阻擋了某些洄游魚種。

questions.passage:
Counting the people who live in a city sounds like arithmetic, but every method produces a different answer. A census counts residents at a fixed address on one night, which misses people with no address, undercounts those who fear officials, and records students and seasonal workers wherever they happen to be sleeping. Administrative data, drawn from tax or health records, catches some of these people but misses anyone outside those systems and double-counts anyone registered twice.

The gaps are not random, which is what makes them consequential. Undercounting is concentrated among renters, recent migrants and the very poor, precisely the groups whose needs drive the funding formulas that the count determines. A district undercounted by five per cent receives five per cent less for schools and clinics for a decade, which tends to increase the conditions that produced the undercount in the first place.

Mobile phone data offers a different picture: it shows where people actually are at each hour, revealing that the working population of a city centre can be three times its residential population. Several statistical offices now publish both figures. The complication is ownership and consent, since the data belongs to telecommunications companies and was collected for billing rather than for public statistics. Cities that have tried to buy it have found the price rises once the seller understands how badly it is needed.

o: A census records people at a fixed address on a single night.
Undercounting falls disproportionately on renters and recent migrants.
Mobile phone data is collected specifically for official statistics.
A city centre's daytime population can be far larger than its residential population.
why: Stated in the first paragraph: a census counts residents at a fixed address on one night.
Stated: undercounting is concentrated among renters, recent migrants and the very poor.
The passage says the data was collected for billing, not for public statistics.
Stated: the working population of a city centre can be three times its residential population.
The passage says administrative data double-counts anyone registered twice.

questions.passage:
A street tree in a European city lives, on average, between seven and twenty years. The same species in a park nearby will live for a century. The difference is almost entirely below ground. A mature tree needs a volume of soil roughly equal to the volume of its crown, and a pavement planting pit typically provides a fraction of that, surrounded by material compacted deliberately so that the paving does not subside.

Compaction is the central problem. Roots cannot penetrate soil beyond a certain density, so they circle inside the pit, exhaust it and then starve. Water is the second problem, and it is not simply scarcity: rain runs off the sealed surface into drains, while the small quantity that does reach the pit often carries road salt. A tree that survives these conditions is then pruned to clear signs and windows, which removes the leaf area it needs to recover.

The engineering solutions are known and are not exotic. Structural soil, a mix of stone and earth in which the stones carry the load and the gaps hold roots, allows planting under paving. Suspended pavements achieve the same by holding the slab on supports above uncompacted ground. Both cost more at installation than a simple pit and less over the life of the tree, which is a calculation that municipal budgeting, divided into annual cycles, finds difficult to make.
questions.q: Which of the following are stated in the passage?
o: Street trees typically live far shorter lives than park trees of the same species.
The main obstacle for roots is soil compacted to stop paving subsiding.
Rainfall reaching street trees is often contaminated with road salt.
Structural soil and suspended pavements are cheaper to install than simple pits.
Street trees are rarely pruned, because they stay small enough to clear signs and windows.
why: Stated in the opening: seven to twenty years in a street against a century in a park.
Stated: soil is compacted deliberately so the paving does not subside, and roots cannot penetrate it.
Stated: the small quantity of water reaching the pit often carries road salt.
The passage says both cost more at installation and less over the tree's life.
The passage says the opposite: street trees are pruned to clear signs and windows, which removes leaf area they need.

zh.A street tree in a European city lives,: 歐洲城市裡的行道樹平均只能活七到二十年。同一樹種若種在附近的公園，卻能活上一個世紀。差別幾乎完全在地面之下。一棵成熟的樹所需的土壤體積，大致等於其樹冠的體積，而人行道上的植穴通常只提供其中一小部分，而且周圍的材料是刻意壓實的，以免路面下陷。
zh.Compaction is the central problem. Roots: 壓實是核心問題。土壤密度超過一定程度後根系就無法穿透，於是根在植穴內繞圈、耗盡養分，接著挨餓。水是第二個問題，而且不只是水量不足：雨水從封閉的路面流進排水溝，而少量進到植穴的水往往帶著道路除冰鹽。能在這些條件下存活的樹，接著又會為了清出標誌和窗戶的視線而被修剪，失去它復原所需的葉面積。
zh.The engineering solutions are known and: 工程上的解方早已為人所知，而且並不稀奇。結構土是石塊與土壤的混合物，由石塊承重、縫隙容納根系，使得鋪面底下也能種樹。懸浮式鋪面則是把路面板架在支柱上，下方保留未壓實的土壤，達到同樣效果。兩者的施工成本都高於簡單的植穴，但以樹木一生來算反而較低，而這種計算對以年度為週期編列的市政預算而言，並不容易做。
