zh.When England introduced a small charge o: 2015 年英格蘭在大型商店對一次性塑膠袋收取少量費用時，一些批評者認為這筆費用太小，起不了作用。結果證明他們錯了。短短幾年內，主要超市售出的塑膠袋數量減少了百分之九十以上。行為經濟學家指出，費用的多寡不如費用的存在本身重要。在收費之前，塑膠袋是免費的，所以拿一個袋子完全不需要做任何決定。一旦附加了價格，無論多小，購物者都必須有意識地做出選擇，於是許多人開始自備購物袋。這項收費也改變了社會規範，讓人覺得每次都被看到買新袋子有點難為情。
zh.According to the passage, why was the sm: 根據文章，為什麼這筆小額收費如此有效？
zh.The charge was large enough to make bags: 這筆費用高到讓人買不起塑膠袋。
zh.Shoppers had to make a conscious choice,: 購物者必須有意識地做出選擇，而且社會規範也改變了。
zh.Supermarkets stopped offering plastic ba: 超市完全停止提供塑膠袋。
zh.The law banned customers from bringing t: 法律禁止顧客自備購物袋。
zh.The passage stresses that the charge was: 文章強調費用很小："the size of the charge was less important than its existence"。
zh.Correct. With any price attached, “shopp: 正確。只要附加了價格，"shoppers had to make a conscious choice"，而且這項收費 "also changed social norms"。
zh.Not stated. Bags were still sold, just f: 文章沒有提到。塑膠袋仍然有販售，只是數量少了很多。
zh.The reverse. “many began bringing their: 正好相反。"many began bringing their own bags"。

questions.passage: When Mount Vesuvius erupted in 79 CE, the town of Pompeii was buried under several metres of volcanic ash. The disaster preserved an extraordinary snapshot of daily Roman life: bread left in ovens, graffiti on walls and the outlines of people caught as they tried to flee. Excavations began in the eighteenth century, but early digging was often careless, driven by the search for treasure rather than an interest in ordinary life. Today archaeologists face a different problem. About a third of the site has never been excavated, and many experts argue it should be left that way, since the exposed ruins are deteriorating from weather, vegetation and the pressure of millions of tourists, and future techniques may reveal far more than current ones.
questions.q: Why do many experts believe part of Pompeii should remain unexcavated?
o: The unexcavated areas contain nothing of interest.
Exposed ruins deteriorate, and future methods may reveal more.
Early excavators have already removed all the treasure.
Tourists are not allowed to visit the site.
why: Not stated, and it would make the argument pointless: experts want to preserve the area because of what it may reveal.
Correct. The exposed ruins “are deteriorating from weather, vegetation and the pressure of millions of tourists, and future techniques may reveal far more”.
The passage says early digging searched for treasure, but not that all of it was removed, and this is not the experts’ reason.
The reverse. The ruins are under pressure from “millions of tourists”.

zh.When Mount Vesuvius erupted in 79 CE, th: 西元 79 年維蘇威火山爆發時，龐貝城被埋在數公尺深的火山灰下。這場災難保存了羅馬人日常生活的一個非凡剪影：留在烤爐裡的麵包、牆上的塗鴉，以及試圖逃跑時被困住的人的輪廓。挖掘工作始於十八世紀，但早期的挖掘往往很草率，動機是尋找寶藏，而不是對日常生活感興趣。如今，考古學家面臨的是另一個問題。遺址約有三分之一從未被挖掘過，而許多專家認為應該維持原狀，因為已經暴露在外的遺跡正因天氣、植物生長以及數百萬遊客帶來的壓力而逐漸損壞，而且未來的技術可能會揭示比現在的技術多得多的東西。
zh.Why do many experts believe part of Pomp: 為什麼許多專家認為龐貝有一部分應該保持不挖掘？
zh.The unexcavated areas contain nothing of: 尚未挖掘的地區沒有任何值得研究的東西。
zh.Exposed ruins deteriorate, and future me: 暴露在外的遺跡會損壞，而且未來的方法可能揭示更多東西。
zh.Early excavators have already removed al: 早期的挖掘者已經把所有寶藏都拿走了。
zh.Tourists are not allowed to visit the si: 遊客不被允許參觀這個遺址。
zh.Not stated, and it would make the argume: 文章沒有這樣說，而且這會讓論點失去意義：專家想保留這個區域，正是因為它可能揭示的東西。
zh.Correct. The exposed ruins “are deterior: 正確。暴露在外的遺跡 "are deteriorating from weather, vegetation and the pressure of millions of tourists, and future techniques may reveal far more"。
zh.The passage says early digging searched: 文章說早期的挖掘是在尋寶，但沒有說寶藏已全部被拿走，而且這也不是專家的理由。
zh.The reverse. The ruins are under pressur: 正好相反。遺跡正承受 "millions of tourists" 帶來的壓力。

questions.passage: In a well-known experiment, volunteers tasted several wines while lying in a brain scanner and were told the price of each one. In fact, two of the glasses contained the same wine, presented once as cheap and once as expensive. Participants not only said they preferred the wine they believed was expensive; activity also increased in a region of the brain linked to the experience of pleasure. The result suggests that expectations do not merely bias what people report but can change what they actually experience. Marketers have long relied on this effect, but it also has implications for medicine, where studies have found that patients sometimes report greater pain relief from a placebo they are told is costly.
questions.q: What does the experiment suggest?
o: Expensive wine is chemically different from cheap wine.
Information about price can change how pleasant something actually feels.
People lie about their preferences when they know they are being observed.
Brain scanners make wine taste better.
why: The experiment used the same wine twice, so there was no chemical difference at all.
Correct. Brain activity linked to pleasure rose, so expectations “can change what they actually experience”, not just what people report.
The passage argues against this: expectations “do not merely bias what people report”.
Nothing suggests the scanner affected taste; the only thing that varied was the stated price.

zh.In a well-known experiment, volunteers t: 在一項著名的實驗中，志願者躺在腦部掃描儀中品嚐幾種葡萄酒，並被告知每一種的價格。事實上，其中兩杯裝的是同一種酒，一次被說成便宜的，一次被說成昂貴的。受試者不僅說他們比較喜歡自以為昂貴的那杯酒；大腦中與愉悅感受有關的區域活動也增加了。這個結果顯示，預期不只會使人們所報告的內容產生偏差，還能改變他們實際的感受。行銷人員長久以來一直利用這種效應，但它對醫學也有啟示：研究發現，病人有時會表示，被告知價格昂貴的安慰劑能帶來更大的止痛效果。
zh.Expensive wine is chemically different f: 昂貴的葡萄酒在化學成分上與便宜的葡萄酒不同。
zh.Information about price can change how p: 價格資訊能改變某樣東西實際帶來的愉悅感受。
zh.People lie about their preferences when: 人們在知道自己被觀察時，會謊報自己的偏好。
腦部掃描儀會讓葡萄酒嚐起來更好喝。
zh.The experiment used the same wine twice,: 這項實驗用的是同一種酒兩次，所以完全沒有化學上的差異。
zh.Correct. Brain activity linked to pleasu: 正確。與愉悅有關的大腦活動增加了，所以預期 "can change what they actually experience"，而不只是改變人們所報告的內容。
zh.The passage argues against this: expecta: 文章反對這種看法：預期 "do not merely bias what people report"。
zh.Nothing suggests the scanner affected ta: 文中沒有任何跡象顯示掃描儀影響了味道；唯一改變的只有所告知的價格。

questions.passage: Robotic rovers have explored Mars for more than two decades, drilling rocks, analysing soil and sending back thousands of images. Advocates of human missions argue that a trained geologist could achieve in a week what a rover achieves in a year, because people can make quick judgements, move freely and respond to the unexpected. Critics reply that sending humans would cost many times more, since astronauts need air, food, water, radiation protection and a way to return home, and that the money could fund dozens of robotic missions. There is also the risk of contaminating Mars with Earth microbes, which could make it impossible to tell whether any life found there was native. For now, most space agencies see robots and humans as complementary, with robotic missions preparing the ground for eventual human exploration.
questions.q: According to the passage, what is the view of most space agencies?
o: Human missions should replace robotic missions as soon as possible.
Robotic missions are pointless because humans work much faster.
Robots and humans have complementary roles, with robots preparing the way for human missions.
Mars should never be visited because of the risk of contamination.
why: This goes beyond the advocates’ argument and is not the agencies’ view; they see the two as working together.
The speed argument belongs to advocates of human missions, and the passage never calls robotic missions pointless.
Correct. “most space agencies see robots and humans as complementary, with robotic missions preparing the ground for eventual human exploration.”
Contamination is raised as a risk, not as a reason never to go; the agencies expect “eventual human exploration”.

zh.Robotic rovers have explored Mars for mo: 機器人探測車探索火星已經超過二十年，它們鑽探岩石、分析土壤，並傳回了數千張影像。支持載人任務的人認為，一位受過訓練的地質學家一週就能完成探測車一年的工作量，因為人類能迅速做出判斷、自由移動，並應付意料之外的狀況。批評者則回應說，派人前往的成本會高出許多倍，因為太空人需要空氣、食物、水、輻射防護以及返回地球的方法，而這些錢足以資助數十次機器人任務。此外，還有用地球微生物污染火星的風險，這可能讓人無法判斷在那裡發現的任何生命是否為火星原生的。目前，大多數太空機構把機器人和人類視為互補的角色，由機器人任務為最終的載人探索鋪路。
zh.According to the passage, what is the vi: 根據文章，大多數太空機構的看法是什麼？
zh.Human missions should replace robotic mi: 載人任務應該盡快取代機器人任務。
zh.Robotic missions are pointless because h: 機器人任務毫無意義，因為人類的工作速度快得多。
zh.Robots and humans have complementary rol: 機器人和人類扮演互補的角色，由機器人為載人任務鋪路。
zh.Mars should never be visited because of: 因為有污染的風險，人類永遠不應該造訪火星。
zh.This goes beyond the advocates’ argument: 這超出了支持者的論點，也不是太空機構的看法；它們認為兩者應該相輔相成。
zh.The speed argument belongs to advocates: 速度的論點來自載人任務的支持者，而文章從未說機器人任務毫無意義。
zh.Correct. “most space agencies see robots: 正確。"most space agencies see robots and humans as complementary, with robotic missions preparing the ground for eventual human exploration."
zh.Contamination is raised as a risk, not a: 污染被提出來是一種風險，而不是永遠不去的理由；太空機構預期會有 "eventual human exploration"。

questions.passage: Ask anyone to recall a review of their work and they will quote the criticism rather than the praise, even when the praise filled four paragraphs and the criticism one line. Psychologists call this negativity bias, and it is among the most reliable findings in the field: bad feedback is processed more thoroughly, remembered longer and weighted more heavily in later judgements. The usual explanation is evolutionary, since the cost of ignoring a threat was historically larger than the cost of ignoring an opportunity. That account is plausible but hard to test, and it is often stretched to explain far more than the evidence supports. What the research does establish is the ratio. Studies of workplaces and of marriages converge on roughly five positive interactions to one negative as the point at which a relationship is experienced as good, which is not a formula so much as a reminder that praise and criticism are not equal units. The practical implication is modest: criticism should be specific and rare enough to be heard, and praise frequent enough to be believed, which is almost the opposite of how most feedback is delivered.
questions.q: What does the passage suggest about negativity bias?
o: It shows that criticism is more accurate than praise.
It is well established, though its evolutionary explanation is harder to verify.
It has been disproved by studies of workplaces and marriages.
It means feedback should consist mainly of criticism.
why: The passage never claims criticism is more accurate, only that it carries more weight.
This matches the text: the bias is among the most reliable findings, while the evolutionary account is called plausible but hard to test.
Those studies support the bias by establishing a ratio; they do not disprove it.
The practical implication given is the opposite: criticism should be rare and specific, praise frequent.

zh.Ask anyone to recall a review of their w: 請任何人回想別人對自己作品的評語，他們引述的會是批評而不是讚美，即使讚美寫了四段、批評只有一行。心理學家稱之為負面偏誤，而它是這個領域中最可靠的發現之一：負面回饋被處理得更徹底、記得更久，在日後的判斷中也佔更大的分量。常見的解釋是演化上的，因為在歷史上忽略威脅的代價，大於忽略機會的代價。這個說法看似合理，卻難以驗證，而且常被延伸去解釋遠超過證據所能支持的範圍。研究確實建立起來的，是比例。對職場與婚姻的研究都指向大約五次正面互動對一次負面互動，是一段關係被體驗為良好的分界點；與其說這是公式，不如說它提醒我們：讚美與批評並不是等量的單位。實務上的啟示並不複雜：批評應該具體，而且要罕見到讓人聽得進去；讚美則要頻繁到讓人願意相信——這幾乎與大多數回饋的給法完全相反。
zh.What does the passage suggest about nega: 本文對負面偏誤的看法是什麼？
zh.It shows that criticism is more accurate: 它顯示批評比讚美更準確。
zh.It is well established, though its evolu: 它已被充分確立，不過它的演化解釋較難驗證。
zh.It has been disproved by studies of work: 職場與婚姻的研究已經推翻了它。
zh.It means feedback should consist mainly: 它意味著回饋應該以批評為主。
zh.The passage never claims criticism is mo: 文章從未主張批評比較準確，只說它分量較重。
zh.This matches the text: the bias is among: 這與文意相符：這個偏誤是最可靠的發現之一，而演化上的說法被形容為合理卻難以驗證。
zh.Those studies support the bias by establ: 那些研究是以比例來支持這個偏誤，並沒有推翻它。
zh.The practical implication given is the o: 文中給出的實務啟示正好相反：批評要罕見而具體，讚美要頻繁。

questions.passage: Brainstorming was introduced in the 1950s on the premise that a group, told to generate ideas freely and withhold criticism, would produce more and better ideas than the same people working alone. It is now among the most studied techniques in organisational psychology, and the finding has been consistent for sixty years: groups brainstorming together produce fewer ideas than the same number of individuals thinking separately and then pooling what they wrote. Three mechanisms account for the gap. Only one person can speak at a time, so the others wait and forget; the presence of colleagues makes some people cautious whatever the rules say; and the group tends to converge early on a line of thought, which narrows the search. None of this means the meeting is worthless. Groups are good at evaluating ideas, at combining two half-formed suggestions and at committing to a decision. The sensible arrangement therefore separates the stages: individuals generate in silence, the group develops and selects, and the facilitator resists the urge to run the first stage aloud because it feels more collaborative.
questions.q: What is the author's view of group brainstorming?
o: It produces more ideas than individuals working separately.
It should be abandoned, since meetings add nothing.
It is weak at generating ideas but useful for developing and choosing them.
Its failure is caused entirely by people fearing criticism.
why: The passage states the opposite: groups produce fewer ideas than the same number of individuals.
The author explicitly says the meeting is not worthless and lists what groups do well.
This matches the conclusion: generate individually, then develop and select as a group.
Caution is only one of three mechanisms; waiting to speak and early convergence are the others.

zh.Brainstorming was introduced in the 1950: 腦力激盪在一九五○年代被提出，前提是一群人若被告知可以自由發想、暫不批評，產出的點子會比同樣這些人各自作業時更多也更好。它如今是組織心理學中最常被研究的技巧之一，而六十年來的結果始終一致：一起腦力激盪的團體所產出的點子，少於同樣人數各自思考後再把所寫內容彙整的成果。造成這個落差的機制有三個。一次只能有一個人說話，其他人只能等待並遺忘；同事在場會讓某些人變得謹慎，不論規則怎麼說；而團體往往很早就收斂到同一條思路上，壓縮了搜尋的範圍。這些都不代表開會毫無價值。團體擅長評估點子、把兩個半成形的建議結合起來，以及作出承諾性的決定。因此合理的安排是把階段分開：個人安靜地發想，團體負責發展與篩選，而主持人要忍住把第一階段拿出來「大家一起講」的衝動——儘管那樣感覺比較有協作感。
zh.What is the author's view of group brain: 作者對團體腦力激盪的看法是什麼？
zh.It produces more ideas than individuals: 它產出的點子比各自作業的個人更多。
zh.It should be abandoned, since meetings a: 應該放棄，因為開會毫無作用。
zh.It is weak at generating ideas but usefu: 它不擅長產生點子，但有助於發展與挑選點子。
zh.Its failure is caused entirely by people: 它之所以失敗，完全是因為人們害怕被批評。
zh.The passage states the opposite: groups: 文章說的正好相反：團體產出的點子少於同樣人數的個人。
zh.The author explicitly says the meeting i: 作者明確表示開會並非毫無價值，並列舉了團體擅長的事。
zh.This matches the conclusion: generate in: 這與結論相符：先個別發想，再由團體發展與篩選。
zh.Caution is only one of three mechanisms;: 謹慎只是三個機制之一，另外還有輪流發言的等待與過早收斂。

questions.passage: Few road safety measures are as unpopular, or as well evidenced, as the speed camera. Studies that simply compare crashes before and after installation tend to overstate the benefit, because cameras are usually placed where crashes have just spiked, and such spikes partly reverse on their own. Once that effect is accounted for, the measured reduction in injury collisions near a camera is smaller but still substantial, in the region of twenty to twenty-five per cent. The objection that cameras are a revenue-raising exercise is answered oddly by the data: in jurisdictions where signage is clear and locations are published, income falls year on year as drivers adapt, which is what a safety measure should do and what a revenue measure would not. A more serious criticism concerns displacement. Drivers brake sharply at the camera and accelerate afterwards, so some of the risk moves a few hundred metres down the road. Average-speed systems, which time a vehicle between two points, remove that behaviour and show larger effects, though they cost more to install and raise sharper questions about continuous monitoring.
questions.q: What does the passage conclude about speed cameras?
o: They reduce injury collisions, though simple comparisons overstate the effect.
They are primarily a means of raising revenue.
They have no measurable effect once statistical corrections are applied.
Average-speed systems are cheaper and less intrusive than fixed cameras.
why: This matches the text: before-and-after studies overstate the benefit, but a substantial reduction remains after correction.
The passage argues against this, noting income falls as drivers adapt.
The reduction is smaller after correction but still around twenty to twenty-five per cent.
The passage says average-speed systems cost more and raise sharper questions about monitoring.

zh.Few road safety measures are as unpopula: 很少有道路安全措施像測速照相一樣既不受歡迎、又證據充分。單純比較設置前後事故數的研究往往高估了效益，因為照相機通常設在事故剛暴增的地點，而這類暴增本來就會部分自行回落。把這個效應納入校正之後，照相機附近傷害事故的降幅較小，但仍相當可觀，大約在兩成到兩成五之間。「照相機只是為了增加收入」這項質疑，被資料以奇特的方式回應了：在標示清楚、地點公開的轄區，收入逐年下降，因為駕駛會調整行為——這正是安全措施該有的結果，而不是增加收入的措施會有的結果。比較嚴肅的批評在於位移效應。駕駛在照相機前急踩煞車，過了之後再加速，因此部分風險只是往前挪了幾百公尺。區間測速系統以兩點之間的行車時間計算速度，可以消除這種行為，效果也更顯著，不過安裝成本較高，對於持續監控也引發更尖銳的問題。
zh.What does the passage conclude about spe: 本文對測速照相的結論是什麼？
zh.They reduce injury collisions, though si: 它們能減少傷害事故，不過單純的前後比較會高估效果。
zh.They are primarily a means of raising re: 它們主要是增加財政收入的手段。
zh.They have no measurable effect once stat: 經過統計校正之後，它們沒有可測量的效果。
zh.Average-speed systems are cheaper and le: 區間測速系統比固定式照相更便宜，侵擾性也更低。
zh.This matches the text: before-and-after: 這與文意相符：前後比較會高估效益，但校正後仍有可觀的降幅。
zh.The passage argues against this, noting: 文章反駁了這一點，指出收入會隨駕駛調整行為而下降。
zh.The reduction is smaller after correctio: 校正後降幅較小，但仍有約兩成到兩成五。
zh.The passage says average-speed systems c: 文章說區間測速系統成本較高，並引發更尖銳的監控問題。

questions.passage: The belief that each learner has a style — visual, auditory or kinaesthetic — and learns best when taught in that style is held by the great majority of teachers in every country where the question has been asked. It is also, as far as the evidence goes, false. The claim makes a testable prediction: students classified as visual learners should do better when taught visually than when taught aurally, and the reverse for auditory learners. Dozens of studies have run that test, and the interaction does not appear. What does appear is that nearly everyone learns better when the material is presented in the form that suits the material: geography in maps, a piece of music by hearing it, a procedure by doing it. The persistence of the myth is itself interesting. It is intuitive, since people do have preferences; it is flattering, since it tells a struggling student that the fault lies in the teaching; and it has an industry behind it selling questionnaires and training. Dislodging it is hard precisely because the preference is real, even though the benefit is not.
questions.q: What is the author's position on learning styles?
o: Teaching should always match the student's preferred style.
Preferences are real, but matching teaching to them does not improve learning.
The theory has never been tested properly.
Students learn best when material is taught in their weakest style.
why: The passage says the predicted benefit does not appear in testing.
This matches the closing line: the preference is real, even though the benefit is not.
The passage says dozens of studies have run the crucial test.
The author argues material should be presented in the form that suits the material, not the student's weakest style.

zh.The belief that each learner has a style: 認為每位學習者都有自己的風格——視覺、聽覺或動覺——而且用該風格教學時學得最好，這種信念在所有被調查過的國家中都為絕大多數教師所持有。然而就證據而言，它是錯的。這個主張提出了可檢驗的預測：被歸類為視覺型的學生，用視覺方式教應該比用聽覺方式教學得更好，聽覺型則反之。數十項研究做過這個檢驗，而這種交互作用並未出現。真正出現的是：當教材以適合「教材本身」的形式呈現時，幾乎每個人都學得更好——地理用地圖、音樂用聆聽、操作程序用實作。這個迷思的頑強本身就很耐人尋味。它直覺，因為人確實有偏好；它讓人寬慰，因為它告訴學習吃力的學生，問題出在教法；而且背後還有一整個販售問卷與師訓的產業。要撼動它之所以困難，正是因為偏好是真的，儘管好處並不存在。
zh.What is the author's position on learnin: 作者對「學習風格」的立場是什麼？
zh.Teaching should always match the student: 教學應該永遠配合學生偏好的風格。
zh.Preferences are real, but matching teach: 偏好確實存在，但讓教學配合它並不能改善學習。
zh.The theory has never been tested properl: 這個理論從未被妥善檢驗過。
zh.Students learn best when material is tau: 學生以自己最弱的風格學習時效果最好。
zh.The passage says the predicted benefit d: 文章說檢驗中並未出現所預測的效益。
zh.This matches the closing line: the prefe: 這與結尾相符：偏好是真的，儘管好處並不存在。
zh.The passage says dozens of studies have: 文章說已有數十項研究做過關鍵檢驗。
zh.The author argues material should be pre: 作者主張教材應以適合教材本身的形式呈現，而不是用學生最弱的風格。

questions.passage: Reducing class sizes is the most popular education reform among parents and among teachers, and one of the least efficient uses of money that research has examined. The best evidence comes from an experiment in Tennessee in the 1980s, which randomly assigned pupils to classes of about fifteen or about twenty-three. The smaller classes produced a real gain, concentrated in the first two years of school and among disadvantaged pupils, and some of the advantage was still measurable years later. The difficulty is arithmetic. Cutting every class from twenty-three to fifteen requires about half as many teachers again, and in a system that already struggles to recruit, the new posts are filled by candidates who would not otherwise have been hired. Several studies find that this quality effect cancels most of the size effect. The alternative, spending the same money on fewer but better-supported teachers, is less visible to parents and harder to campaign for, which is why the reform most often enacted is the one the evidence supports least.
questions.q: What does the author conclude about reducing class sizes?
o: It produces no benefit at any age.
It works, so systems should reduce every class to fifteen pupils.
It helps, especially early and for disadvantaged pupils, but recruiting enough teachers erodes the gain.
Tennessee's experiment was too small to be informative.
why: The passage reports a real gain in the early years and among disadvantaged pupils.
The author points out that staffing every class at fifteen draws in weaker teachers, cancelling most of the benefit.
This matches the argument: a genuine effect, offset by the quality of the additional teachers required.
The Tennessee study is described as the best evidence available, not as too small.

zh.Reducing class sizes is the most popular: 縮小班級規模是家長與教師都最支持的教育改革，也是研究所檢視過的用錢方式中效率最低的做法之一。最有力的證據來自一九八○年代田納西州的一項實驗，它把學生隨機分配到約十五人或約二十三人的班級。小班確實帶來成效，集中在入學頭兩年以及弱勢學生身上，其中部分優勢在多年後仍可測量到。困難在於算術。把每個班從二十三人降到十五人，需要多出約一半的教師，而在一個本就招不滿人的體系裡，新增的職缺會由原本不會被錄取的人選填補。多項研究發現，這種素質效應抵消了大部分的規模效應。另一種選擇——把同樣的錢用在人數較少但支援更充分的教師身上——對家長而言比較不顯眼，也比較難拿來倡議，這就是為什麼最常被推行的改革，正是證據最不支持的那一個。
zh.What does the author conclude about redu: 作者對縮小班級規模的結論是什麼？
它在任何年齡都沒有效益。
zh.It works, so systems should reduce every: 它有效，因此各體系都應把每班降到十五人。
zh.It helps, especially early and for disad: 它有幫助，尤其在低年級與弱勢學生身上，但招募足夠教師會侵蝕這項效益。
zh.Tennessee's experiment was too small to: 田納西州的實驗規模太小，無法提供有用資訊。
zh.The passage reports a real gain in the e: 文章指出低年級與弱勢學生確實有實際的成效。
zh.The author points out that staffing ever: 作者指出，要讓每班都維持十五人會引進素質較差的教師，抵消大部分效益。
zh.This matches the argument: a genuine eff: 這與論點相符：效果真實存在，但被所需增聘教師的素質抵消。
zh.The Tennessee study is described as the: 文中把田納西州的研究形容為現有最佳證據，而不是規模太小。

questions.passage: Speed reading courses promise a tripling of reading rate with no loss of comprehension, and the claim has been tested often enough to be settled. The eye does not move smoothly along a line; it jumps between fixations, and each jump takes a fixed minimum time that training does not shorten. Readers can be taught to make fewer fixations, and this does raise words per minute, but above roughly four hundred words a minute comprehension falls in direct proportion to the gain. What the fastest demonstrators are doing is skimming, a genuinely useful skill with a different purpose: locating what matters in a text rather than understanding all of it. The honest version of the advice is therefore narrower than the sales pitch. Skim deliberately when surveying a field, read slowly when the argument is difficult, and recognise that the main avoidable waste is not slow eye movement but re-reading sentences because attention wandered. That problem is solved by removing interruptions, not by moving the eyes faster.
questions.q: What does the passage say about speed reading?
o: Training can triple reading speed without harming comprehension.
Beyond a certain speed, gains come at the cost of comprehension, and fast readers are skimming.
Eye movements are the main cause of slow reading.
Skimming is of no practical value.
why: The passage states that above about four hundred words a minute comprehension falls in proportion.
This matches the text: comprehension falls beyond that rate, and the fastest demonstrators are skimming.
The passage says the main avoidable waste is re-reading because attention wandered, not eye movement.
Skimming is called a genuinely useful skill with a different purpose.

zh.Speed reading courses promise a tripling: 速讀課程承諾在不損失理解力的前提下把閱讀速度提高三倍，而這個說法已被檢驗得夠多次，足以下定論。眼睛並不是沿著一行平順移動，而是在注視點之間跳躍，每一次跳躍都有固定的最短時間，訓練無法縮短它。讀者可以被訓練成減少注視次數，這確實能提高每分鐘字數，但超過大約每分鐘四百字之後，理解力會與速度的增加成正比地下降。那些示範得最快的人其實是在略讀，而略讀是一種確實有用、但目的不同的技巧：它是為了找出文章中重要的部分，而不是理解全部。因此，誠實版本的建議比銷售說詞窄得多。在概覽一個領域時刻意略讀，在論證困難時放慢速度，並且認清：真正可以避免的浪費不是眼動太慢，而是因為分心而重讀句子。那個問題要靠排除干擾來解決，而不是靠讓眼睛移動得更快。

questions.passage: Predictions of a cashless society have been made since the 1960s, and cash keeps not disappearing. Its share of transactions has certainly collapsed in several countries: in Sweden and Norway fewer than one payment in ten is now made with notes and coins, and many shops no longer accept them. Yet the value of currency in circulation has risen almost everywhere, including in those countries, because cash has two jobs. As a means of payment it is losing; as a store of value, held in safes and under mattresses against crisis or inflation, it is gaining. The policy question is not whether cash will vanish but what a society owes the people who rely on it. Those are disproportionately the old, the very poor and victims of domestic financial control, for whom a card leaves a record a partner can see. Several central banks have concluded that a purely private payment system is a vulnerability in any case, since a network failure or a commercial decision could cut off a whole population, which is one of the arguments behind proposals for a public digital currency.

questions.title: Lecture: how habits work
questions.text: Much of what we do each day is not the result of conscious decisions at all. Studies that ask people to record their actions every hour suggest that around forty per cent of daily behaviour is habitual, performed in the same context without deliberate thought. Habits form through a simple loop: a cue in the environment, a routine that follows it, and a reward that reinforces the connection. Over time, the brain shifts control of the routine from regions involved in planning to regions involved in automatic behaviour, which is why habits feel effortless. This has an important implication for anyone trying to change their behaviour. Because habits are triggered by cues, willpower is a poor tool for breaking them; it works for a while and then fails when we are tired or stressed. A more reliable strategy is to change the environment, removing the cue for an unwanted habit or making a desired behaviour easier to start. People who succeed in changing habits, the research suggests, rarely have more self-control than others. They simply arrange their surroundings so that they need it less.

the brain shifts control to automatic regions, so habits feel effortless

change the environment: remove cues and make good behaviours easier
questions.model: The lecturer explained that around forty per cent of daily behaviour is habitual, formed through a loop of cue, routine and reward, as the brain shifts control to automatic regions. Because habits are triggered by cues, willpower is unreliable for changing them. questions.title: Lecture: the bridge that wobbled
questions.text: When the Millennium Bridge opened in London in 2000, it began to sway sideways as soon as crowds walked across it, and it was closed after just two days. The engineers had checked the bridge for vertical vibration, which is the usual concern with footbridges, but not for this sideways movement. The cause turned out to be the interaction between the bridge and the people on it. When a bridge sways slightly, pedestrians instinctively adjust their steps to keep their balance, and in doing so they start walking in time with the movement. That pushes the bridge further in the same direction, which makes more people fall into step, creating a feedback loop. Crucially, the effect appeared only once the number of people passed a critical threshold. The solution was to fit dampers, devices that absorb energy, under the deck, and the bridge reopened two years later. The episode changed design codes for footbridges around the world.

engineers had checked vertical vibration but not sideways movement
pedestrians adjusted their steps and fell into time with the sway, creating a feedback loop
the effect appeared only above a critical number of people

Dampers solved the problem, and design codes worldwide changed.

questions.title: Lecture: spacing your study
questions.text: If you have ten hours to prepare for an exam, how should you divide them? Most students cram, spending most of the time in the last day or two. More than a century of research on memory suggests this is one of the least efficient strategies available. The spacing effect, first described in the 1880s, shows that the same amount of study produces much longer-lasting memory when it is spread out over time. The reason seems to be that forgetting a little between sessions forces the brain to work harder to retrieve information, and that effort strengthens the memory. Cramming can produce good results the next morning, which is why students keep doing it, but most of what is learned disappears within weeks. The best gap depends on how long you need to remember the material: for an exam in a week, reviewing every day or two works well, while for knowledge needed in a year, gaps of several weeks are better. In practice, spacing is simple to apply, but it requires starting early.

questions.title: Lecture: the cane toad
questions.text: In 1935, around one hundred cane toads were brought from Hawaii to north-eastern Australia to control beetles that were damaging sugar cane crops. The plan failed almost completely. The beetles lived high on the cane stalks, where the toads could not reach them, and the toads found plenty of other food instead. With no natural predators in Australia and the ability to lay tens of thousands of eggs at a time, the toads spread rapidly. Today there are estimated to be more than two hundred million of them, and their range expands by up to fifty kilometres a year. The damage comes mainly from their poison. Native predators such as quolls, goannas and freshwater crocodiles, which have never encountered toads before, often die after trying to eat one. Scientists are now experimenting with conditioned taste aversion, feeding predators small, non-lethal pieces of toad that make them sick, so they learn to avoid the real thing. The episode is still taught as a warning about introducing species without understanding the ecosystem.

questions.title: Lecture: counting the unemployed
questions.text: Unemployment sounds like something you could simply count, but every figure you have seen rests on a definition that excludes somebody. The standard international measure counts you as unemployed only if you are out of work, available to start, and have actively looked for a job in the past four weeks. Fail the last test and you vanish from the statistics: a person who has given up after two years of rejection is not unemployed, they are outside the labour force. That is why the headline rate can fall during a bad recession, as discouraged workers stop searching, and rise during a recovery, when they start again. A second problem is underemployment. Someone working six hours a week who wants forty is counted as employed, exactly like a full-time engineer. Economists therefore publish a family of measures rather than one, and the gap between the narrowest and the widest can be eight percentage points. When a politician quotes an unemployment figure, the useful question is not whether it is accurate but which of these measures it is.

people who give up searching leave the statistics entirely
so the rate can fall in a recession and rise in a recovery
underemployment is hidden: six hours a week counts as employed

The headline rate can therefore fall during a recession and rise in a recovery. Underemployment is also hidden, since someone working six hours a week counts as employed. Economists publish several measures, which can differ by about eight percentage points.

zh.Unemployment sounds like something you c: 失業聽起來像是可以直接數出來的東西，但你看到的每一個數字，背後都有一個會排除某些人的定義。國際上的標準指標，只有在你沒有工作、隨時可以上工，而且過去四週內積極找過工作時，才把你算成失業。最後一項不符合，你就從統計中消失了：一個被拒絕兩年後放棄的人並不算失業，而是被歸為非勞動力。這就是為什麼在嚴重衰退期間，隨著灰心的求職者停止尋找，失業率反而可能下降；而在復甦期間，當他們重新開始找工作時，失業率反而上升。第二個問題是未充分就業。一個每週工作六小時、卻想工作四十小時的人，和一位全職工程師一樣被算成就業。因此經濟學家公布的是一整組指標，而不是單一數字，其中最窄與最寬的定義之間可以相差八個百分點。當政治人物引用失業數字時，值得問的不是它準不準，而是它屬於哪一種指標。

questions.title: Lecture: before anaesthesia
questions.text: It is difficult now to imagine surgery without anaesthesia, but for most of history that is exactly what surgery was. Speed was the only mercy available, and the best surgeons were judged by the clock: one London operator could remove a leg in under thirty seconds. Patients who survived the operation often died of infection afterwards, which was not understood until decades later. Ether changed this in 1846, when a Boston dentist demonstrated it publicly and a surgeon removed a tumour from a patient who felt nothing. News crossed the Atlantic in weeks, which tells you how badly the problem needed solving. What is less often told is what anaesthesia then made possible, and what it cost. Surgeons could now work slowly and reach places they had never dared enter, so operations became longer, deeper and far more frequent. Without antiseptic practice, which arrived twenty years later, the result was a rise in deaths from infection. The lesson is not that the discovery was a mistake, but that a technique which removes one limit often exposes the next.
keys: before 1846, surgery was done without anaesthesia and judged on speed
ether was demonstrated publicly in Boston and spread within weeks
anaesthesia let surgeons operate slowly and deeply for the first time
operations became longer and more frequent
without antiseptics, deaths from infection rose for twenty years
questions.model: The lecturer explained that before 1846 surgery was performed without anaesthesia, so speed was the only mercy and the best surgeons were judged by the clock. The public demonstration of ether in Boston spread within weeks. Anaesthesia then allowed slower, deeper and more frequent operations, but because antiseptic practice arrived twenty years later, deaths from infection rose in the meantime.

zh.before 1846, surgery was done without an: 一八四六年以前，外科手術沒有麻醉，醫師以速度論高下
zh.ether was demonstrated publicly in Bosto: 乙醚在波士頓公開示範，數週內便傳開

zh.The lecturer explained that before 1846: 講者說明，一八四六年以前的外科手術沒有麻醉，速度是唯一的仁慈，最好的外科醫師以碼錶論高下。乙醚在波士頓的公開示範，數週之內就傳遍各地。麻醉接著讓手術得以緩慢、深入且更頻繁地進行，但由於消毒法要再過二十年才出現，這段期間因感染而死亡的人數反而上升。
zh.It is difficult now to imagine surgery w: 今天很難想像沒有麻醉的外科手術，但在歷史上大部分時間，手術就是如此。速度是唯一能給的仁慈，最優秀的外科醫師是用碼錶來評斷的：倫敦一位名醫可以在三十秒內切除一條腿。熬過手術的病人往往死於術後感染，而這一點要到數十年後才被理解。一八四六年，乙醚改變了這一切：波士頓一位牙醫公開示範，一名外科醫師為毫無感覺的病人切除了腫瘤。消息在幾週之內傳過大西洋，可見這個問題有多迫切需要解決。比較少被提到的是，麻醉接著讓什麼成為可能，又付出了什麼代價。外科醫師現在可以慢慢動刀，深入從前不敢進入的部位，於是手術變得更長、更深入，也更頻繁。在二十年後消毒法出現之前，結果是死於感染的人數上升。這個教訓並不是說這項發現是個錯誤，而是說：解除一個限制的技術，往往會讓下一個限制顯露出來。

questions.title: Lecture: the trouble with averages
questions.text: In the 1950s the United States Air Force had a puzzle: pilots were crashing planes that were working perfectly. The cockpits had been designed in the 1920s around the average measurements of hundreds of pilots, so the fit should have been good. A young researcher measured four thousand pilots on ten dimensions and asked a simple question: how many were within the middle range on all ten? The answer was none. Not one pilot was average across the board, and fewer than four per cent were average on even three dimensions at once. The cockpit had been designed for a person who did not exist. The fix was not a better average but adjustable seats, pedals and straps, which is why your car has them today. The general lesson reaches well beyond aircraft. Averages describe a population, not any member of it, and whenever a system is designed for the average user, it tends to fit nobody particularly well. Where adjustment is cheap, design for range rather than for the middle.

of four thousand pilots, none was average on all ten dimensions
under four per cent were average on even three
the fix was adjustable seats and controls, not a better average
averages describe a population, not any individual in it
questions.model: The lecturer described how 1950s air force cockpits, designed around average pilot measurements, fitted nobody: of four thousand pilots measured on ten dimensions, none was average on all of them and fewer than four per cent on even three. The solution was adjustable seats and controls rather than a better average. Averages describe populations, not individuals, so systems should be designed for range.

zh.The lecturer described how 1950s air for: 講者描述一九五○年代空軍座艙依照飛行員平均尺寸設計，結果誰都不合身：在以十個維度測量的四千名飛行員中，沒有一位在全部維度上都屬於平均，連三個維度同時落在平均範圍的也不到百分之四。解決之道是可調整的座椅與操縱裝置，而不是更精確的平均值。平均值描述的是群體而非個人，因此設計應該為「範圍」而做。
zh.In the 1950s the United States Air Force: 一九五○年代，美國空軍遇到一個難題：飛行員駕駛完全正常的飛機卻發生墜機。座艙是在一九二○年代依據數百名飛行員的平均尺寸所設計的，照理說應該相當合身。一位年輕研究員測量了四千名飛行員的十項身體尺寸，並提出一個簡單的問題：有多少人在這十項上都落在中間範圍？答案是：一個也沒有。沒有任何一位飛行員在所有項目上都屬於平均，甚至連三項同時落在平均範圍的也不到百分之四。那座艙是為一個並不存在的人設計的。解決方法不是更精確的平均值，而是可調整的座椅、踏板和安全帶，這也是你今天的汽車上會有這些裝置的原因。這個教訓的適用範圍遠遠超出飛機。平均值描述的是一個群體，而不是其中任何一位成員；每當一套系統是為「平均使用者」設計時，它往往對誰都不特別合適。只要調整的成本不高，就該為範圍而設計，而不是為中間值。

questions.text: Welcome to the second week of term. I want to take a few minutes to explain how the writing centre works, because every year students discover it only a week before their dissertation is due, which is far too late to be useful. The centre offers one-to-one appointments of forty-five minutes with a trained tutor. You can book up to two appointments a week through the student portal, and I strongly recommend booking early, because slots fill up quickly after the middle of term. Please be clear about what the tutors will and will not do. They will help you plan an essay, organise an argument and understand feedback you have received from your lecturers. They will not proofread your work line by line, and they will not tell you what mark it is likely to receive. If you bring a draft, bring a printed copy and a specific question, such as whether your conclusion follows from your evidence. The centre also runs drop-in workshops on Wednesday afternoons on topics like referencing and paraphrasing. These do not need to be booked, but they are limited to twenty students, so arrive on time. Finally, the centre is free for all students, including those studying part-time or online, and online students can hold their appointments by video call.

questions.text: When cities plan for hotter summers, the first tool they usually reach for is air conditioning, but there is growing evidence that trees deserve far more attention. A mature street tree cools its surroundings in two ways. Its canopy shades pavements and walls, which would otherwise absorb heat all day and release it at night. And its leaves release water vapour, which cools the air in the same way that sweat cools skin. Measurements in several European cities have found that streets with continuous tree cover can be up to five degrees cooler at pedestrian level than similar streets without trees. The benefits are not only thermal. Tree-lined streets have been linked with lower levels of stress, and some studies suggest that people walk more where streets are shaded. However, planting a tree is not the same as growing one. In many cities, a large share of newly planted trees die within the first few years, usually because they are not watered during dry summers or because their roots have too little space under the pavement. For that reason, experts increasingly argue that budgets should be measured not by the number of trees planted, but by the number that survive to maturity, which can take twenty years or more.

Streets with continuous tree cover can be up to five degrees cooler at pedestrian level.
Air conditioning is more effective than trees at reducing night-time heat.

questions.text: Most people assume that when they put plastic in a recycling bin, it will become a new plastic product. In reality, only a small fraction of plastic is ever recycled; global estimates put the figure at under ten per cent. There are several reasons. First, plastic is not one material but many, and different types cannot usually be melted together. A single yoghurt pot may combine two or three plastics, which makes it almost impossible to recycle. Second, each time plastic is recycled, its quality declines, so it is often turned into lower-value products, such as park benches, that cannot themselves be recycled again. Third, and most importantly, recycled plastic has to compete on price with new plastic made from oil and gas. When oil prices fall, new plastic becomes cheaper and demand for recycled material collapses. For many years, wealthy countries dealt with this by exporting their plastic waste to Asia, until China banned most imports in 2018. Since then, attention has shifted towards reducing plastic use in the first place, and towards designing packaging from a single type of plastic that is easier to process. Neither approach is a complete solution, but both are more effective than simply buying a larger recycling bin.

questions.text: Good morning, everyone. With the exam period starting in two weeks, I want to go through the arrangements, because they have changed slightly this year. Second, you need to bring your student card. If you have lost it, you can get a temporary replacement from the student office, but this takes two working days, so do not leave it until the morning of the exam. Mobile phones must be switched off and placed in the clear plastic bags provided at the entrance; they cannot be kept in pockets, even if they are switched off. Water is allowed, but only in a transparent bottle with the label removed. Finally, if you are ill on the day of an exam, do not come in. Contact the exams office before the exam starts and submit a medical certificate within five days, and you will be offered a place in the resit period without penalty.

questions.text: When coffee arrived in Europe in the seventeenth century, it did more than change what people drank. It created a new kind of public space. The first coffeehouse in England opened in Oxford in 1650, and within a few decades London had hundreds of them. For the price of a single cup, anyone could sit for hours, read newspapers and join conversations, regardless of social rank. That openness made coffeehouses centres of information. Merchants met in them to exchange news about ships and cargoes, and several important institutions grew out of particular coffeehouses: one became a famous insurance market, and another was the origin of the London Stock Exchange. Scientists also used them for informal debate, and some were nicknamed penny universities, because the conversation was said to be as educational as a university course. Not everyone approved. In 1675, the king attempted to close them all, claiming they spread false rumours about the government, but the order caused such an outcry that it was withdrawn within days. Historians sometimes describe coffeehouses as an early version of social media: noisy, influential, and difficult for the authorities to control. Their influence is a reminder that new places to meet can change how ideas spread.

questions.text: If you have ever compared the price you paid for a flight with the person sitting next to you, you may have discovered a large difference. Airlines use a system called yield management, which divides the seats on a flight into many price levels, sometimes more than twenty. The cheapest levels are released first and sell out, and as the departure date approaches, the remaining seats move into higher price bands. The logic is that people who book early, such as holidaymakers, are usually sensitive to price, while those who book late, often business travellers, are more willing to pay. Airlines also adjust prices according to demand, so a flight during the school holidays will cost more than the same flight a week later. A common belief is that airlines raise prices when you search for the same flight several times, using information stored in your browser. Investigations have found little evidence for this; the rises people notice usually happen because cheaper seats have genuinely sold out in the meantime. For travellers, the practical advice is simple: book early for popular dates, and be flexible if you can. Flying midweek, rather than on a Friday or Sunday, is often noticeably cheaper as well.
questions.q: Which points does the speaker make?
o: Late bookers are usually the most price-sensitive customers.
Seats on one flight may be sold at many different price levels.
Flights during school holidays tend to cost more.
There is strong evidence that repeated searches make prices rise.
Price rises during a search are usually caused by cheaper seats selling out.

questions.text: This session is about finding and evaluating sources for your essays. Most of you will start with a general search engine, and that is fine for getting an overview, but the results are ranked partly by popularity, not reliability. For academic work, you should move on to the library databases, which you can access through the library website with your university login, including from home. When you find a source, ask four questions. Who wrote it, and what are their qualifications? When was it published? In fast-moving fields, a study from fifteen years ago may be out of date. What evidence does it use, and can you check it? And why was it written: to inform, or to sell something? Peer-reviewed journal articles are usually the most reliable, but peer review is not a guarantee, so you still need to read critically. Wikipedia is a useful starting point for background and for its reference lists, but you should not cite it in your essays; follow its references to the original sources instead. Finally, keep a record of everything you read as you go, including page numbers. Trying to find a quotation again the night before a deadline is a frustrating experience that many of you will otherwise have.
questions.q: Which of the following does the speaker recommend?
o: Using the library databases, which can be accessed from home.
Relying mainly on search engine rankings to judge reliability.
Checking when a source was published.

questions.text: Elephants communicate using a remarkable range of sounds, but many of their calls cannot be heard by humans at all. These are infrasonic rumbles, pitched below the lower limit of human hearing. Low-frequency sounds lose little energy as they travel, so these rumbles can carry for several kilometres, particularly in the cool, still air of early morning and evening. Researchers first became aware of them in the 1980s, when a scientist standing near captive elephants noticed a strange throbbing in the air, similar to the feeling of distant thunder. Recording equipment later confirmed that the animals were producing sounds too low to hear. Elephants appear to use these calls to coordinate the movements of family groups that are out of sight of one another, and females use them to signal to males when they are ready to mate. There is also evidence that elephants detect vibrations through the ground, possibly using sensitive cells in their feet and trunks. Understanding these calls has practical value: conservationists now use listening devices in forests to monitor elephant populations, since the animals are far easier to hear than to see. The same recordings can also warn villages when elephants are approaching their crops.

Elephants may sense vibrations through the ground.

zh.Infrasonic rumbles can travel only a few: 次聲波的隆隆聲只能傳播幾公尺。

questions.text: The London Underground, which opened in 1863, was the first underground railway in the world. The first line ran for about six kilometres between Paddington and Farringdon, and it was built using a method called cut and cover: workers dug a deep trench along the route of an existing road, built the tunnel, and then covered it over again. This caused enormous disruption, but it was cheaper than tunnelling. The early trains were pulled by steam locomotives, and although special engines were designed to reduce smoke, the tunnels were famously dirty and filled with fumes. Despite this, the railway was an immediate success, carrying tens of thousands of passengers on its first day. Later lines were built much deeper using tunnelling shields, which allowed workers to dig safely through the London clay without disturbing the streets above. These deep tunnels became usable for passengers only after the introduction of electric trains in the 1890s, since steam engines could not be used in narrow tunnels so far underground. The circular shape of these deep tunnels is why Londoners still call the Underground the Tube. Today the network carries several million passengers every day.

o: The first line was built by digging a trench and covering it over.

The name the Tube comes from the round shape of the deep tunnels.

zh.Which of the following are true accordin: 根據這場講座，下列哪些是正確的？
zh.The first line was built by digging a tr: 第一條路線是以挖溝再覆蓋的方式建造的。
zh.The early tunnels were clean because the: 早期的隧道很乾淨，因為列車不會產生煙霧。
zh.The railway was unpopular when it first: 這條鐵路剛開通時並不受歡迎。
zh.Deep tunnels became usable once electric: 引進電力列車後，深層隧道才得以使用。
zh.The name the Tube comes from the round s: 「管子」這個名稱來自深層隧道的圓形外觀。
zh.The London Underground, which opened in: 1863 年通車的倫敦地鐵，是世界上第一條地下鐵路。第一條路線在帕丁頓和法靈頓之間延伸約六公里，採用一種稱為「明挖覆蓋法」的方式建造：工人沿著一條現有道路的路線挖出一條深溝，建好隧道，然後再把它覆蓋起來。這造成了極大的干擾，但比鑽掘隧道便宜。早期的列車由蒸汽機車牽引，雖然設計了特殊的引擎來減少煙霧，但隧道還是出了名地骯髒、充滿廢氣。儘管如此，這條鐵路一開通就大獲成功，第一天就載運了數萬名乘客。後來的路線利用隧道盾構機建得更深，讓工人能安全地穿過倫敦黏土層挖掘，而不會干擾上方的街道。這些深層隧道直到 1890 年代引進電力列車之後，才能用來載客，因為蒸汽機車無法在位於地下這麼深的狹窄隧道中使用。這些深層隧道的圓形外觀，就是倫敦人至今仍把地鐵稱為「管子」的原因。如今，這個路網每天載運數百萬名乘客。

questions.text: Before we finish the orientation, I want to tell you about the support that is available if you find things difficult this year, because many students only look for it when a problem has become serious. The student wellbeing centre offers free, confidential counselling. You can refer yourself online; you do not need a letter from a doctor or a tutor, and most students are seen within a week. If you need to talk to someone urgently, there is a drop-in service every weekday between twelve and two, and outside those hours the university runs a phone line that is staffed twenty-four hours a day. Counselling is not only for serious crises. Students come to us about homesickness, stress before exams, relationship problems and difficulties with sleep. We also run group workshops, for example on managing anxiety and on studying effectively, which are a good way to learn practical skills alongside other students. If you have a disability or a long-term health condition, please register with the disability service as early as possible, even if you are not sure you will need support, because arrangements such as extra time in exams can take several weeks to put in place.

questions.text: Today I want to walk you through how a gallery decides that a painting is what it claims to be, because the process is less dramatic and more interesting than the films suggest. There are three kinds of evidence, and no serious attribution rests on one alone. The first is provenance: the documented chain of ownership. A painting with an unbroken paper trail back to the artist's studio is in a far stronger position than one that appears from a private collection with no history before 1950, which is a period gap that should always make you cautious. The second is connoisseurship, the judgement of specialists who have looked at hundreds of works by the same hand. This is the part outsiders distrust most, and it is genuinely fallible, but it is also how most forgeries are first doubted. The third is science. Pigment analysis can show that a colour was not manufactured until two centuries after the supposed date; dendrochronology can date the panel; infrared reflectography reveals the drawing underneath, and forgers rarely bother to make the underdrawing convincing, because they do not expect anyone to look. Science can usually prove a painting false. What it cannot do is prove one genuine, since the best a laboratory can say is that nothing in the materials is inconsistent with the claimed date. That asymmetry is worth remembering whenever you read that a work has been scientifically authenticated.

zh.The lecture says science can disprove bu: 講座說科學通常能證偽，卻無法證明一幅畫是真跡。
zh.Today I want to walk you through how a g: 今天我想帶各位走過一遍：美術館如何判定一幅畫就是它所宣稱的那一幅，因為這個過程沒有電影演得那麼戲劇化，卻更有意思。證據有三類，而任何嚴謹的歸屬判定都不會只靠其中一類。第一類是來源：有文件可考的所有權鏈。一幅能一路回溯到畫家工作室、紀錄不曾中斷的作品，地位遠強於一幅突然從私人收藏冒出來、一九五○年以前毫無歷史的作品，而那樣的空白期永遠值得警覺。第二類是鑑賞，也就是看過同一位畫家數百件作品的專家所下的判斷。這是外行人最不信任的部分，它確實可能出錯，但大多數偽作最初也正是因此被懷疑的。第三類是科學。顏料分析可以顯示某種顏色要到宣稱年代的兩個世紀之後才被製造出來；年輪定年可以判斷木板的年代；紅外線反射成像能揭露底下的素描，而偽造者很少費心把底層素描做得令人信服，因為他們根本不認為有人會去看。科學通常能證明一幅畫是假的。它做不到的是證明一幅畫是真的，因為實驗室最多只能說：材料中沒有任何東西與宣稱的年代相牴觸。每當你讀到某件作品「已通過科學鑑定」時，這個不對稱性都值得記住。

questions.text: Before you leave, there are three changes to coursework submission that start on Monday, and I would rather you heard them from me than discovered them at two in the morning on a deadline. First, everything now goes through the new portal. The old email address is closed, not monitored, so an essay sent there is not late, it simply does not exist. Second, the portal timestamps on upload, not on submission of the form, which sounds like a technicality but is not: if you start uploading a large file at 23:58 and it finishes at 00:03, the system records it as late. Leave yourself half an hour, not five minutes. Third, and this is the one people get wrong, extensions are now requested through the same portal rather than from me. I cannot grant one by email, and if you ask me in the corridor, I will tell you to use the form, which will feel unhelpful but protects you, because a request in the system is logged and a conversation is not. The penalty itself has not changed: five per cent a day, up to five days, and after that a mark of zero. One thing that has changed in your favour is that the portal now shows a receipt with the exact upload time. Save it. In the three disputes we had last year, the student was right in two, and we only knew because they had the receipt.

questions.text: A tall building does not fall over in a storm; it sways, and the problem engineers worry about is not collapse but motion that people can feel. Above about forty storeys, a building moving even a few centimetres at the top makes occupants queasy, in much the way a ship does. The simplest answer is to make the structure stiffer, but stiffness is expensive, it adds weight and a heavier building needs deeper foundations. So from the 1970s engineers borrowed an idea from mechanical engineering: the tuned mass damper. Near the top of the tower you hang an enormous weight, often several hundred tonnes, on cables or bearings, and you tune its natural period to match the building's. When the tower moves one way, the weight lags behind and pulls the other way, and the sway is damped rather than resisted. The building in Taipei has a visible golden sphere of six hundred and sixty tonnes, which has become a tourist attraction in its own right. Water tanks can do the same job more cheaply, using the sloshing of the liquid, and they double as a fire reserve. What none of these systems does is make the building safer in an earthquake, which is a common misunderstanding. They are tuned to the slow sway of wind; an earthquake shakes a building much faster and in a different mode, and the damper simply cannot respond in time.

Tuned mass dampers protect buildings during earthquakes.
why: Stated: the problem is not collapse but motion that people can feel.
The lecture says stiffness is expensive and adds weight.
Stated: the weight is tuned so its natural period matches the building's.
Stated: water tanks do the job more cheaply and double as a fire reserve.
The lecture explicitly calls this a common misunderstanding.

questions.text: People often ask who decides when a new word goes into the dictionary, and the honest answer is that nobody decides to admit it; editors simply notice that it is already there. A large dictionary runs on a corpus, a database of billions of words of published and spoken English, and the first signal is frequency: a candidate word has to appear often enough, across enough different sources, over enough years. Three criteria matter. The word must be widespread, meaning it is not confined to one magazine or one city. It must be sustained, which usually means several years of use, because a word tied to a single news event tends to vanish with it. And it must be meaningful in the sense that writers use it without explaining it, which is the clearest evidence that readers are expected to know it. Editors do not judge whether a word is ugly, or whether the thing it names is desirable. Inclusion is not approval, and this is the point that generates angry letters. When a dictionary added a slang term for a social media behaviour last year, several correspondents wrote to say that the word was not real English. The editors' reply is always the same: the dictionary records the language that exists, not the one anybody would prefer. The judgement they do make is about space, since every edition has a fixed number of pages, and the words that leave are usually technical terms nobody now needs.

questions.text: Two announcements about getting around campus, both starting after the holiday. The first concerns the shuttle bus. From the fifth, it runs every ten minutes instead of every twenty between eight and ten in the morning, and every twenty for the rest of the day, which is the reverse of the current pattern. We looked at the counts and the morning buses were leaving people standing at the gate while the two o'clock service ran almost empty. The last bus is unchanged at eleven. The second change is the bike scheme. We are moving from the free loan system, which lost about forty bikes a term, to a deposit model: twenty pounds, refunded when you return the bike at the end of the year. I know that looks like a charge, and for a few of you it is a real obstacle, so there is a hardship waiver through the student centre, no questions asked beyond the standard form. The racks outside the library are being doubled, and three of the new stands will take cargo bikes, which several of you asked for. One thing we have not solved is lighting on the path behind the sports hall, which is the complaint we receive most often. The estates budget for this year is committed, so the honest answer is that it will be next September, and until then I would use the longer route by the main road after dark.

questions.text: Students are often unsettled the first time a clinical guideline they have learned is reversed, so I want to say something about why that happens and why it is usually a good sign. A guideline is not a statement of fact; it is the best available summary of evidence at a moment, weighted by how confident we are in each study. When a large, well-designed trial reports, the summary can shift. The advice on infant sleeping position is the clearest example. For decades parents were told to place babies face down, which came from reasonable-sounding theory about choking and from observation in hospitals. When population studies eventually tested it, the reverse turned out to be true, and campaigns to put babies on their backs cut sudden infant deaths by more than half. The failure there was not that the advice changed; it was that it had been given with such confidence before it had been tested. Two habits follow for your own practice. First, read the strength of a recommendation, not just its direction, because guidelines mark which rest on strong evidence and which on expert opinion, and the second kind changes often. Second, when a patient tells you that the advice used to be the opposite, agree with them. They are right, and a clinician who pretends otherwise loses the credibility they need the next time the evidence moves.

questions.text: The periodic table is usually introduced as a filing system, which undersells what Mendeleev actually did. By 1869 chemists had isolated about sixty elements and knew their atomic weights, and several people had noticed that properties seemed to repeat at intervals. What distinguished Mendeleev was his willingness to trust the pattern over the data. Where an element did not fit, he left a gap rather than forcing it in, and he predicted the properties of what should occupy that gap, including density and melting point. When gallium was isolated six years later, its measured density differed from his prediction, and Mendeleev wrote to say that the measurement must be wrong. It was: the sample was impure, and the corrected figure matched. He also reversed two elements whose atomic weights contradicted their chemistry, which was criticised at the time and turned out to be right for a reason nobody could know, since the ordering principle is the number of protons rather than weight. What he could not explain was why the pattern existed at all. That had to wait fifty years for quantum mechanics and the structure of electron shells. It is worth remembering that the table was useful, and correct in its predictions, for half a century before anyone understood the reason behind it.

地震很少直接致人於死；大多數的死亡是由倒塌的建築物造成的。因此，工程師發展出好幾種讓建築更安全的技術。其中最有效的一種是「隔震」，讓建築物坐落在能吸收大部分地面晃動的彈性支承上。另一種是加裝大型阻尼器，在強烈搖晃時減少高樓的擺動。在許多國家，嚴格的建築法規現在規定新建築必須具備這些設計，不過舊建築往往仍有風險。
